## Sprint 11ad — S124 Arrange-contract + clip drift closure (ArrangeCore / child-wins-then-clip / conditional clip / Arrange-entry WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S124 arrange contract — `Arrange(finalRect) → final_rect` + the render-slot clip — matches the real WPF source's `ArrangeCore`/`Arrange`/`GetLayoutClip` semantics; the S124 audit residual drift removed)  [token S832+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S124 dep:S123 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit):** the S124 arrange contract + clip was audited against the actual WPF source (`E:\GitRepos\wpf`, `PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs`) and found to drift on the ARRANGE + CLIP SEMANTICS — three clusters of fidelity defects, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture arrange/clip behavior WPF does not have):
> - **Arrange-squeeze (MATERIAL) — the child-wins-then-clip strategy is INVERTED.** WPF `FrameworkElement.ArrangeCore` explicitly arranges a squeezed child at its **full `unclippedDesiredSize`, NOT a smaller size**, and records `NeedsClipBounds = true` so the renderer clips the overflow later — `arrangeSize = finalRect.Size` start (FE.cs:4539), margin-reduced (FE.cs:4547-4548), then the replace-if-smaller rule at **FE.cs:4595-4606** (`if (DoubleUtil.LessThan(arrangeSize.Width, unclippedDesiredSize.Width)) { NeedsClipBounds = true; arrangeSize.Width = unclippedDesiredSize.Width; }`), the non-Stretch fall-back `arrangeSize = unclippedDesiredSize` (FE.cs:4617-4623), and the clientSize-vs-clippedInkSize clip flag (FE.cs:4681-4687). The arrange contract comment is explicit: *"we will not actually arrange a child at a smaller size … so lets replace the smaller arrange size with UnclippedDesiredSize and then clip the guy later"* (FE.cs:4522-4531). VAML's `compute_final_rect` (LayoutSlot.cpp/h) instead **clamps the child to `min(desired, available)`** (non-Stretch) or `available` (Stretch) — it **shrinks the child to fit the slot, so overflow never exists to clip**. This is the **inverse** of WPF's strategy: WPF keeps the child big + clips; VAML makes the child small so nothing overflows. `clip_to_bounds` (S124) is thereby a near-no-op in the arrange flow (there is no overflow to feed it), and the whole "clip bounds honored by render slot" promise is vacuous.
> - **Clip (MATERIAL) — unconditional vs WPF's conditional `NeedsClipBounds`/`ClipToBounds` gate.** WPF's clip is computed by `ensureClip` at the end of `Arrange` (UIElement.cs:884 → 3056) and `GetLayoutClip` (base UIElement.cs:3322; FrameworkElement.cs:4862), and is applied **only when `NeedsClipBounds` is true or `ClipToBounds` is true** — a fitting element gets `null` (no clip at all). VAML's `clip_to_bounds` (LayoutSlot.cpp:139, LayoutSlot.h) clips **unconditionally** (always intersects), and there is **no `NeedsClipBounds` state machine and no `ClipToBounds` DP**. So the "when" the clip applies is wrong, and the explicit WPF opt-in flag is absent.
> - **Arrange-entry (minor) — no `Arrange` guard spectrum.** WPF `UIElement.Arrange` (a) throws `InvalidOperationException` on an Inf/NaN slot (UIElement.cs:798-809), (b) short-circuits a `Visibility.Collapsed` / layout-suspended element — records `_finalRect` but returns WITHOUT arranging (UIElement.cs:811-828), (c) backfills `Measure` when `MeasureDirty || NeverMeasured` (UIElement.cs:833-862), and (d) calls `ensureClip(finalRect.Size)` at the end (UIElement.cs:884-901). VAML `UIElement::Arrange` (src/core/src/UIElement.cpp) does none of these: an infinite `arrangeSlot` silently produces garbage `final_rect_`; a Collapsed element is arranged normally; a never-measured element is arranged with a stale/zero `desired_size_`; and no clip is applied at arrange (S829 fixes the *Measure* entry only — the arrange-side entry is NOT covered).
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint):** close each cluster on the WPF-observable contract. **Arrange keeps the child at its unclipped desired size when the slot squeezes it**, setting a needs-clip flag instead of shrinking the child — restoring WPF's "child wins then clip" so `clip_to_bounds` has real overflow to honor; the **render-slot clip becomes conditional** on that flag (or an explicit `ClipToBounds` DP), matching `NeedsClipBounds`/`GetLayoutClip`; and **`Arrange` gains the WPF entry spectrum** (Inf/NaN guard + Collapsed skip + measure-on-arrange backfill + ensureClip at the end). Each resolves the exact drift, no invented surface is added.

## Sprint 11ae — S126/S127 layout-driver drift closure (Invalidate / RenderSize / override-seam WPF-fidelity)  [token S839+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S126 dep:S125 + S127 dep:S126 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against E:\GitRepos\wpf PresentationCore\System\Windows\UIElement.cs + LayoutManager.cs + PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs):** the S126 dirty-flag/invalidation/LayoutManager contract and the S127 MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride seam carry SEVEN axes of conversion-blocker drift (S128/S129/S131/S134/S136 + S208 depend on the divergent model). The migration contract (a commercial app moves WPF → VAML with ZERO behavioral modifications) admits no partial credit, so each is a mandatory close, not optional debt:
> **D1 INVALIDATION — up-propagation at invalidate time vs. WPF's desired-size waterfall.** VAML InvalidateMeasure/InvalidateArrange walk the parent chain marking every ancestor dirty (UIElement.cpp). WPF sets ONLY the local bit + adds the element to the MeasureQueue (UIElement.cs:249-274); ancestors become dirty lazily, ONLY when an actual DesiredSize change fires OnChildDesiredSizeChanged (UIElement.cs:688-698; default :323-327, gated on IsMeasureValid). VAML over-invalidates unconditionally → is_measure_dirty()/is_arrange_dirty() observables differ from WPF.
> **D2 INDEPENDENCE — measure/arrange "independent axes" vs. WPF's coupling.** WPF couples them: Measure calls InvalidateArrange() (UIElement.cs:629-631) and "arrangement cannot be valid without measurement first being valid" (UIElement.cs:222-224). S126's celebrated independence test property is VOID.
> **D3 RENDER-SIZE/INK (material, S208/11r-touching) — ArrangeOverride void(Rect) vs. WPF Size(Size)->RenderSize.** WPF FrameworkElement seals ArrangeCore, computes an arrangeSize, calls ArrangeOverride(arrangeSize) where arrangeSize is Size ~ NOT Rect, sets RenderSize = innerInkSize (the override's return; FrameworkElement.cs:4720-4721); offset is separate via SetLayoutOffset (:4788). The return "can be another size if the panel actually takes smaller/larger than finalSize" (:5101-5102). Clip geometry is built from RenderSize (ink), not the slot (UIElement.cs:3326; NeedsClipBounds triggers :4581-4592/:4668-4674/:4780-4785), and RenderSize feeds ActualWidth/Height (:4804-4806). ## Sprint 11af — S240 PropertyPath grammar drift closure (empty→Direct, /, ^, (), whitespace-in-name)  [token S845+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S240/S242/S244 binding-core audit per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\MS\Internal\Data\PathParser.cs + System\Windows\PropertyPath.cs):** S240's "hand-rolled WPF-faithful grammar" silently dropped operators WPF's parser actually has, and one claim was flatly wrong — the empty-path case. The migration contract (commercial WPF→VAML with zero behavioral change) admits no partial credit, so each is a mandatory close:
> **D1 EMPTY→DIRECT (the flatly-wrong claim).** WPF treats `Path=""` / `Path="."` as a VALID `Direct` self-binding to the whole object — `if (_n == 0) ... return new SourceValueInfo[] { new(Direct, ...) }` (PathParser.cs:83-89) — and a leading `.`/`/`/`[` at State.Init is legal (:103-115). VAML declared empty a Class-A `Empty` error and rejected a leading `.` as `TrailingDot` — the exact opposite of WPF. Direct self-binding (`{Binding}`, no Path) is thereby unconvertible.
> **D2 DRILL-IN OPERATOR — `/` missing.** WPF grammar: each level is `.propname` / `/propname` / `[index]` / `/[index]` (:57-66); `/` = `DrillIn.Always`, `.` = `DrillIn.Never`, first level defaults `IfNeeded` (StartNewLevel resets to `Never`, :127-136/:372). VAML has no `/` at all — `/Items[0]`, `/propname` unconvertible.
> **D3 INDEXER ESCAPE — `^` missing.** WPF `EscapeChar = '^'` escapes `, ( ) ] ^` and whitespace inside indexers (:417, :239-247). VAML's `parse_index_inner` has no escape handling.
> **D4 PAREN STRING + MULTI-PARAM INDEXERS.** WPF indexer is a comma-separated `IndexerParamInfo{parenString, valueString}` list (:17-32, :172-181) with nested `[ [ ] ]`. VAML accepts a single Integer/StringKey only.
> **D5 WHITESPACE-IN-NAME (bonus found in audit).** `IsSpecialChar` is only `.` `/` `[` `]` (:401-405) — a name is read until one of those and `.Trim()`ed (:150-165), so `"First Name"` is a legal property name; internal whitespace is NOT a boundary. VAML's `is_name_break` treats all whitespace as a syntax boundary — WPF-divergent.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close):** the VAML parser is rewritten as the WPF Init→DrillIn→Prop(/Indexer) state machine: empty/`.` → a valid `Direct` (moved OUT of Class-A-error into a valid read that returns the root value; `PropertyPathError::Empty` stays as the stable no-error/ok tag), leading `.`/`/`/`[` accepted, `/` reproduced as `DrillIn.Always` (semantics — drill into a collection/items view — rides in with the collection reader per the recorded NO-GAP, parse is faithful now), `^` escape inside indexers, the comma-separated `(paren)value` param list (multi-param `[i,j]` staged with multi-dim arrays; the single-Integer/StringKey convenience forms are preserved), and internal whitespace legal in names. `{Binding}` with an empty path becomes a valid self-binding. **Relation:** dep:S240; independent of S803's composite DP-key migration (the reader resolves a name against the object; the composite owner resolution is S803's concern). ZERO new locks (ADR-018). ZERO invented names. Supersedes the pre-11af "Empty = Class-A error" S240_1/BindingDiagnostic precondition — recorded, history preserved un-edited.
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** S849 authors the closed surface LIVE in the viewer (S222_1 RELOAD re-demonstrated) — a `{Binding}` with no Path binds the whole DataContext; a collection path resolves through `/`; a property named with an embedded space / a paren key resolves — with the WPF-faithful observable each implies. No token, no ✅ per the S11+ OPEN-ENDED clause. No silent backfill; NO invented names (all WPF-real); ZERO new locks.
- S845 dep:S240  **GRAMMAR STATE-MACHINE REWRITE (D1+D2+D5): WPF-faithful path parser.** Rewrite the parse core as the WPF Init→DrillIn→Prop(/Indexer) loop (PathParser.cs state machine); empty/`.` → valid `Direct` (is_direct()); leading `.`/`/`/`[` accepted at State.Init (:103-115); `/` → `DrillIn.Always`, `.` → `DrillIn.Never`, first level `IfNeeded`, per-level reset to `Never` (StartNewLevel :372); names read until `.`/`/`/`[`/`]` honoring paren-level, then trimmed (internal whitespace legal — D5). `Empty` is retired as a syntax error (kept as the stable no-error/ok tag); Class-A errors are the real remaining arms (UnterminatedIndexer, EmptyIndexer, MalformedIndex, UnclosedQuote, UnmatchedParen). Both CI lanes green from first principles.

Preserve the existing single-Integer/single-StringKey convenience accessors (backward compatible). `[i,j]` multi-param staged with multi-dim arrays as a recorded NOT-CLOSED (per Rule 1, explicit, not silent). Both CI lanes green.

## Sprint 11as — S403 Slider drift closure (RangeBase / ValueChanged routed event / coercion / thumb-drag / DP-inventory WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S403 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "Value/Min/Max DPs (Value clamps to the range); the value-changed Signal + the routed `ValueChanged` event (source==this); the thumb-drag `set_value_from_ratio` mapping a [0,1] drag ratio to Value" — matches the actual WPF source; the S403 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1000+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S403 dep:S402 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\RangeBase.cs` + `...\Controls\Slider.cs` + `...\Controls\Primitives\Track.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` / `src/vulkan/src/VamlRenderer.cpp`):**
> the S403 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on SEVEN observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture Slider behavior WPF does not have). The audit body is the Disciplined `DRIFT-1..7` findings; each is closed here:
> - **D1 (BUG) — the claimed routed `"ValueChanged"` event is NOT the real event.** VAML raises `RoutedEvent::registered("\1", ...)` (`Element.cpp:1907`, and the sibling sites 2013/2063/2081 for CheckBox/ScrollViewer) — an **octal escape `\1` = the control byte `\x01`**, so the event registered/raised is NAMED `\x01`, not `"ValueChanged"`. The registry is content-keyed and dispatch matches handlers by `event.name()`, so a handler subscribed to the real `"ValueChanged"` event never fires. WPF's routed event IS genuinely `"ValueChanged"`: `RangeBase.ValueChangedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("ValueChanged", RoutingStrategy.Bubble, typeof(RoutedPropertyChangedEventHandler<double>), typeof(RangeBase))`. The `value_changed()` **Signal** still fires, but the "routed `ValueChanged` event (source==this)" claim is FALSE — no event named `ValueChanged` is raised by a Slider today.
> - **D2 — default Maximum is 10 in WPF, 100 in VAML; and min/max changes don't re-coerce Value.** WPF `Slider.cs` static ctor `MaximumProperty.OverrideMetadata(typeof(Slider), 10.0)` (Minimum 0.0, Value 0.0); a default Slider spans `[0,10]`. VAML registers `Maximum` default `100.0` (`Element.cpp:1801-1804`). Worse, WPF **re-coerces** `Value` whenever Minimum/Maximum change: `RangeBase.OnMinimumChanged`/`OnMaximumChanged` call `ctrl.CoerceValue(ValueProperty)`, and `CoerceMinimum`/`CoerceMaximum` pin `Min <= Max`. VAML's `set_minimum`/`set_maximum` merely `Set` the DP and never re-clamp the current Value nor enforce `Max >= Min` — `s.set_value(50); s.set_maximum(10)` leaves `Value == 50` (out of range). WPF would coerce Value to 10.
> - **D3 (structural) — no `RangeBase` base, no shared identity.** WPF `Slider : RangeBase : Control`; `Value`/`Minimum`/`Maximum`/`ValueChanged`/`LargeChange`/`SmallChange` all live on **`RangeBase`** (shared with `ScrollBar`/`ProgressBar`). VAML `Slider final : UIElement` flattens them, and `ProgressBar`/`ScrollBar` each re-register their own `("Value", owner)` DPs — under the 11s composite `(name, ownerType)` contract these are THREE DISTINCT DPs where WPF has ONE shared `RangeBase.Value` (`DependencyProperty.FromName("Value", typeof(RangeBase))`).
> - **D4 — Value property flags.** WPF `RangeBase.ValueProperty` is registered `BindsTwoWayByDefault | Journal`, and `Slider` `OverrideMetadata`s it with `AffectsMeasure`. VAML registers `Value` with `PropertyFlags::None` — so a plain `{Binding Value}` on a Slider is NOT two-way by default and a Slider Value change does NOT invalidate measure (the 11aa S819 runtime-effect flag never applies).
> - **D5 — DP inventory deltas.** VAML is missing `Orientation`, `AutoToolTipPlacement`/`AutoToolTipPrecision`, and `LargeChange`/`SmallChange` (WPF defaults 1.0/0.1); the 11k-9 table registered `IsDirectionReversed`/`IsSnapToTickEnabled`/`TickPlacement`/`TickFrequency`/`Ticks`/`IsSelectionRangeEnabled`/`SelectionStart`/`SelectionEnd`/`IsMoveToPointEnabled` as untyped `Int32` guard-only names with no Slider behavior.
> - **D6 — `set_value_from_ratio` is NOT the WPF thumb-drag mapping.** VAML maps a `[0,1]` ratio over the FULL `[Min,Max]` range as an absolute proportion. WPF `Slider.OnThumbDragDelta` is a **delta-accumulation** model: `newValue = Value + Track.ValueFromDistance(dx)` where `ValueFromDistance = scale * delta * Density` and `Density = range / remainingTrackLength` (`Track.ComputeSliderLengths`, `remainingTrackLength = trackLength − thumbLength`); thumb position = `(Value−Min) * Density` over the REMAINING track, and `UpdateValue` calls `SnapToTick` before the clamp when `IsSnapToTickEnabled`.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) real routed event `"ValueChanged"` (the `\1` bug fixed; a handler subscribed to the real event fires); (2) `Maximum` default 10 + `OnMinimumChanged`/`OnMaximumChanged`→`CoerceValue(Value)` re-coercion + `Max>=Min`; (3) a real `vaml::RangeBase` base carrying the shared Value/Min/Max/LargeChange/SmallChange/ValueChanged, with Slider/ProgressBar/ScrollBar re-pointed onto it (the 11s composite-identity shared-owner contract); (4) `Value` carries `BindsTwoWayByDefault` + `AffectsMeasure`; (5) the full Slider/RangeBase DP inventory (add Orientation/AutoToolTip*/LargeChange/SmallChange, promote the 9 stubs to real owner-typed DPs); (6) `set_value_from_ratio` replaced by the WPF `Track.ValueFromDistance` delta model + `IsMoveToPointEnabled` + `SnapToTick`. **DRIFT-7 (rendered chrome — the flat track box vs a full thumb/ticks template) is NOT re-litigated:** it is the S409_1 viewer-growth continuation (the generic `classify_merge_element → the track box` vertical slice stays; the real thumb/chrome renders at S409_1, recorded NO-GAP), exactly as the S480 Label-glyph hand-off stays with S409_1.
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab/11ac/11af/11ai/11ak/11al/11am/11an/11ao/11ap/11aq/11ar/11ag/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity (S800-S808 — the shared `RangeBase.Value` pair-keyed store + the owner re-key); 11t owns the value-pipeline order + wrong-thread throw + the strict-synchronous `with_changed` model; 11aa owns `BindsTwoWayByDefault` runtime effect (S819); 11ab owns the `FrameworkElement` base (S824) + `Control`-branch DP owners (11j-5); 11ai the `vaml::` exception base; 11ak/11al the style/trigger/precedence closures; 11am/11an the ControlTemplate/TemplateBinding closures; 11aq/11ar the S401/S402 residuals this sprint mirrors; **11ag owns the Sprint-8 routed-event/input ENGINE (S870-S877) whose real `"ValueChanged"`-named event dispatch S1001's event fix rides (the event raises through the real routed-event engine; 11ag's class-handler/Direct work is its own seat)**; 11z's executor seam untouched. 11as is independent of 11s/11t/11u (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change) — it closes the S403-Slider-SPECIFIC residual (D1-D6). ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + coerced re-set + encoder, the S126 affinity model unchanged).
> **VIEWER GROWTH (anti-grave-whistle):** this sprint DOES move the viewer — S1007 renders the closed surfaces LIVE: a Slider whose thumb sits at the WPF ratio-based position with `Value` clamped + re-coerced (S1002/S1006), a plain `{Binding Value}` Slider that WRITES BACK two-way-by-default (S1003), and the real `"ValueChanged"` routed event firing on a drag (S1001). ## Sprint 11bx — ContentPresenter base closure (the S1204 prepare-unit host: the WPF-real `ContentPresenter` — the per-item data-context unit 11bw S1204's prepare loop routes through — closed end-to-end)  (goal: the S500/11bw per-item `ContentPresenter` the ItemsControl prepare loop CONSUMES matches the actual WPF `ContentPresenter.cs` public surface on EVERY axis — the `object` `Content` DP, the template/selector/format/source DPs, the WPF default-template DISPATCH (renders Strings/UIElements/objects, never a blank), the DataContext-sync contract, the `PrepareContentPresenter`/`ClearContentPresenter` recycling contract, the single-child measure/arrange helper honor, and the WPF lifetime/reparent model — so the 11bw S1204 `ContentPresenter.PrepareContentPresenter(item, ItemTemplate, ItemTemplateSelector, ItemStringFormat)` hand-off lands on a base that is WPF-true, not the divergent S500 minimal one)  [token S1210+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S500/11bw per-item `ContentPresenter` audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-Source-Audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\ContentPresenter.cs` and the code VAML ships in `src/core/include/vaml/core/ContentPresenter.h` + `src/core/src/ContentPresenter.cpp` (the S500 minimal per-item host the 11bw S1204 prepare loop CALLS), with the composite-identity `(name, ownerType)` (11s), the measure/arrange corrections (11ac/11ad), the RenderSize/ink (11ae), and the `ContentControl`/`Control` base family (11bp/11bq) already woven):**
> the S500/11bw `[DONE]` `ContentPresenter` is the S500 minimal per-item unit — `ContentPresenter : FrameworkElement` with `prepare_content(UIElement*, DataTemplate*)` — and the 11bw S1204 prepare loop CONSUMES it. Auditing the ACTUAL `ContentPresenter.cs` shows the base drifts from the WPF source on SEVEN observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF `ContentPresenter`, and the 11bw S1204 `PrepareContentPresenter(item, ItemTemplate, ItemTemplateSelector, ItemStringFormat)` call must land on a WPF-true host), not recorded debt. S500/11bw authored NOTHING this sprint re-works as "a new element" — it corrects the CONSUMED host in place. Each residual below is audited against the real source:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — the WPF `object` `Content` DP is absent; `prepare_content(UIElement*, ...)` accepts only a `UIElement*`.** WPF `ContentPresenter.cs:169-176` registers `ContentProperty = ContentControl.ContentProperty.AddOwner(typeof(ContentPresenter), ...)` holding an **object** (WPF `ContentControl.Content`, `AffectsMeasure`) — a scalar/String/`UIElement`/any, so `<ContentPresenter Content="..."/>`/`Content="{Binding X}"` (binding an object, incl. a String — the ubiquitous `ContentControl.Content` feeding a CP) expresses an object, not only a `UIElement*`. VAML's `prepare_content(UIElement*)`/no `(Content, ContentPresenter)` DP REFUSES any non-`UIElement` content.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — the template/selector/format/source DPs are absent.** WPF owns `ContentTemplateProperty` (`ContentControl.ContentTemplate.AddOwner`, `AffectsMeasure`, OnContentTemplateChanged :186-203), `ContentTemplateSelectorProperty` (AddOwner :228-245), `ContentStringFormatProperty` (AddOwner :255-296), `ContentSourceProperty` (:298-330 — auto-alias), `RecognizesAccessKeyProperty` (bool :139-157). VAML passes a lone `DataTemplate*` parameter; no DPs. (11k-9 registered these as resolvable names — no step owns the CP-OWNED real surface; this sprint does.)
> - **D3 (MATERIAL — the "renders blank" headline) — the WPF default-template DISPATCH is absent: with NO template, WPF still renders content; VAML renders NOTHING.** WPF `ChooseTemplate`/the `DefaultTemplate` selector (:361-395, :665-728, `DefaultTemplate.DoDefaultExpansion` :558-641) dispatches a `String` → a TextBlock (`SelectTemplateForString`), a `UIElement` → the element directly (`UIElementContentTemplate`), an `XmlNode` → the XML template, an `Inline` → a TextBlock.Inlines, and every other `object` → `String.Format("{0}", content)` in a TextBlock. So `<ContentPresenter Content="hello"/>` renders "hello" in WPF, a BLANK in VAML (S500 `prepare_content` returns `0` when `itemTemplate == nullptr`).
> - **D4 (MATERIAL) — the DataContext-sync contract is assumed, not performed.** WPF `Initialize()` nulls the DataContext ("CP always has local DC", :78) and `OnContentChanged`/`EnsureTemplate` sync `this.DataContext = Content` (:289-297, :572) so the template's `{Binding}` resolves via the inheritable `DataContext` (11ab/S824). VAML's `prepare_content` explicitly does NOT set DataContext ("the caller via set_data_context") — the WPF unit OWNS it.
> - **D5 (MATERIAL) — the `PrepareContentPresenter`/`ClearContentPresenter` recycling contract is absent.** WPF `internal PrepareContentPresenter(object item, DataTemplate, DataTemplateSelector, stringFormat)` + `ClearContentPresenter(object item)` → `Content = DisconnectedItem` (:390-424). 11bw S1204 literally CALLS `ContentPresenter.PrepareContentPresenter(item, ItemTemplate, ItemTemplateSelector, ItemStringFormat)` — that signature does NOT exist on VAML's CP (only `prepare_content(UIElement*, DataTemplate*)`, no selector/stringFormat). This sprint lands the EXACT signature 11bw invokes + the recycling clear.
> - **D6 (measurable) — the single-child measure/arrange helper is NOT honored.** WPF `MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride` delegate to `Helper.MeasureElementWithSingleChild`/`ArrangeElementWithSingleChild` (:339-356) honoring the child's **margin + alignment**. VAML measures the child raw + arranges it to fill. 11ac/11ad/11ae corrected the GENERIC measure/arrange; the CP-vs-`[SingleChild]` helper honor is THIS seat (RE-BASED, not re-authored).
> - **D7 (lifetime) — the WPF lifetime/reparent model is not adopted.** WPF builds template content via `StyleHelper.AddCustomTemplateRoot` under a forgotten content-parent so the content inherits DataContext but not the templated owner's other context (:651-663). > **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S129/S130 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Stack.cs` (the REAL authoritative `StackPanel` — WPF keeps ~one type per `.cs`, `StackPanel` is the known multi-type-file case) and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` ([`StackPanel::MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride`] :2523-2608) / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` (`class StackPanel : FrameworkElement` :225-241), plus the sibling controls' shared-owner squats in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (ScrollBar `set_orientation` :6091-6103, ToolBar `set_orientation` :6514-6526, ToolBarTray `set_orientation` :6686-6697), and cross-checked against `ScrollBar.cs` / `ToolBar.cs` / `ToolBarTray.cs`):** the S129 `[DONE]`/S130 `[DONE]` markers overstate fidelity on the exact surfaces those markers name — and critically **no sibling corrective sprint reaches them**: 11bt closed GridSplitter, 11bz closed Grid (the `Grid : Panel` panel spine), 11bh closed DockPanel, 11cm is the WrapPanel re-audit — but **StackPanel is the ONLY team-B vertical/horizontal stacking panel that never received a per-control drift-closure sprint** (11ab S824 re-based StackPanel onto FrameworkElement but did NOT give it the WPF `Panel : IStackMeasure, IScrollInfo` surface; 11ac/11ad/11ae re-based the generic measure/arrange/driver seams ON which StackPanel rides but closed NONE of the StackPanel-OWN surface), and the `S646` `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S646 StackPanel ×4 xaml instances]` scan queue re-bases on THIS surface. Each residual axis below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF `<StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal" IsScrolling="True">` document and lay out WPF-observably), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — the ARRANGE last-child-stretch is INVENTED: WPF's `StackArrangeHelper` gives EVERY child the identical slot rule with NO last-child special case.** VAML `StackPanel::ArrangeOverride` (`Element.cpp:2575-2608`) computes `const bool isLast = (i + 1 == child_count()); const float remaining = finalSlot.<axis> - <cursor>; const float slot<axis> = isLast ? remaining : child->desired_size().<axis>;` and ADVANCES the cursor by `(isLast ? remaining : child->desired_size().<axis>)` — the LAST child is forced to FILL all remaining space and the cursor jumps by the leftover. WPF `StackArrangeHelper` (Stack.cs — verified above, non-scrolling branch) gives **every** child, INCLUDING the last, the identical rule with NO `IsLast` special case:
> ```csharp
> // StackArrangeHelper — the loop (all children, no last-child branch):
> if (fHorizontal)
> {
>     rcChild.X += previousChildSize;
>     previousChildSize = child.DesiredSize.Width;
>     rcChild.Width = previousChildSize;                       // = child desired, stack axis
>     rcChild.Height = Math.Max(arrangeSize.Height, child.DesiredSize.Height);
> }
> else
> {
>     rcChild.Y += previousChildSize;
>     previousChildSize = child.DesiredSize.Height;
>     rcChild.Height = previousChildSize;                      // = child desired, stack axis
>     rcChild.Width = Math.Max(arrangeSize.Width, child.DesiredSize.Width);
> }
> child.Arrange(rcChild);
> ```
> WPF arranges the last child at its measured DESIRED stack extent exactly like every other child — any "fill the leftover" appearance is achieved INSIDE the child via the child's OWN `Stretch` alignment + `ArrangeCore` (the 11ac/11ad child-wins-then-clip machinery at FE.cs child-wins), NEVER by the panel shrinking/growing the last slot or advancing the cursor by leftover. The S130 test suite (`StackPanel_stretch_test.cpp`, the S129/S130 headline "last-child-stretch" green-on-CI because it asserts VAML's invented behavior) must be re-based to the WPF source. **This is the CORE 11ca drift — the direct `S129`/`S130` DONE-marker-overstatement.**
> - **D2 (STRUCTURAL — the scrolling surface is MISSING): WPF `StackPanel : Panel, IScrollInfo, IStackMeasure` (Stack.cs) — the ENTIRE `StackMeasureHelper`/`StackArrangeHelper` scrolling engine (the `IsScrolling` branch, the `IStackMeasureScrollData.Offset/Viewport/Extent/ComputedOffset`, `SetPhysicalViewport`, `VerifyScrollingData`, `OnScrollChange`, `MakeVisible`, `LineUp/Down`, `PageUp/Down`, `CanVerticallyScroll`/`CanHorizontallyScroll`, the per-viewport logical measure/clamp `stackDesiredSize.Width = Math.Min(desired,constraint)` + `viewPort` estimate) — VAML's `StackPanel` has NONE of it** (verified: `grep IStackMeasure|IScrollInfo|IsScrolling|ScrollData` in `src/` returns ZERO hits — no scrolling branch, no `IStackMeasure`, no `IScrollInfo` anywhere; the `MeasureOverride` has NO `IsScrolling` clamp-and-viewport arm, the `ArrangeOverride` has NO scroll-offset branch). 11bc S1072 / 11au S1021 own the `IScrollInfo` INTERFACE abstraction; **the StackPanel-side `IStackMeasure`/scrolling IMPLEMENTATION is THIS sprint's** (the `StackMeasureHelper` scroll arm + the `ScrollData` model + the `CanVerticallyScroll`/`CanHorizontallyScroll` bools + the scroll-arrange offset) — COORDINATED with, NOT duplicating, the 11bc/11au interface surface. This ALSO re-keys D1's non-scrolling branch correctly: WPF's non-scrolling arrange is the loop above (D1), and the SCROLLING arrange (the ONLY place the "fill/offset" lives) uses the scroll offset — never a bare `isLast` fill.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL — Rule 3 owner/coexistence): `ScrollBar`/`ToolBar`/`ToolBarTray` SQUAT on the StackPanel-owned bare `(Orientation, StackPanel)` DP instead of owning their own.** WPF registers a DISTINCT `(Orientation, <owner>)` per control — `ScrollBar.OrientationProperty` is owned by `ScrollBar` (ScrollBar.cs, `DependencyProperty.Register("Orientation", typeof(Orientation), typeof(ScrollBar), ...)`), `ToolBar.OrientationProperty` by `ToolBar` (ToolBar.cs:109-110 — a `DependencyPropertyKey`-registered READ-ONLY), `ToolBarTray.OrientationProperty` by `ToolBarTray` (ToolBarTray.cs:88-98, default `Horizontal` + `OnOrientationPropertyChanged` → `CoerceValue(ToolBar.OrientationProperty)`), and `StackPanel.OrientationProperty` by `StackPanel` (Stack.cs) — FOUR DISTINCT DPs under the composite `(name, ownerType)` identity (Rule 3). VAML's `Element.cpp` registers `(Orientation, "StackPanel")` ONCE (the `ensure_stackpanel_properties_registered` at :55-63) and ScrollBar/ToolBar/ToolBarTray ALL read/write it via `PropertyId::of("Orientation", "StackPanel")` (ScrollBar :6093-6095, ToolBar :6516-6518, ToolBarTray :6688-6689 ) — the comment itself records the drift (`"Reuses the SHARED GLOBAL bare 'Orientation' property (StackPanel-owner — see register_scrollbar_properties — no ScrollBar.Orientation registration)"`). So `DependencyProperty.FromName("Orientation", typeof(ToolBar))`/`typeof(ToolBarTray)` never resolves, ToolBar's `Orientation` is NOT the read-only coerced-by-tray WPF DP (ToolBarTray's change coerces ToolBar — VAML has no such coupling), and the 11s un-revert (S805) never reached these three siblings. Independent of 11s's `(name, owner)` store — the registrations simply sit at the wrong owner.
> - **D4 (PS — value-type surface): the `Orientation` DP has no `IsValidOrientation` boundary gate + no `AffectsMeasure`/`AffectsParentMeasure`, and `GridLength`-style double plumbing is float.** WPF's four `Orientation` registrations each carry `new ValidateValueCallback(ScrollBar.IsValidOrientation)` (Stack.cs, ScrollBar.cs, ToolBarTray.cs:97) + `AffectsMeasure` (Stack.cs, ScrollBar, ToolBarTray `AffectsParentMeasure`) — an authored `Orientation="3"` is REJECTED (the 11t `S810_1` disposition THROWS `InvalidPropertyValueException`). VAML registers `(Orientation, StackPanel)` with NO validator + NO `AffectsMeasure` (the 11aa S818 flags absent). The `Orientation` enum {Horizontal,Vertical} + the default (Vertical on StackPanel, Horizontal on ScrollBar/ToolBarTray) are WPF-real and HOLDS (D-H-frame) — only the boundary/flag surface drifts.
> **HOLDS (D-H — the part of S129/S130 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened + pinned):** the `Orientation` enum **ordinals** `{Horizontal=0, Vertical=1}` (S11p re-pointed — WPF Orientation.cs, HOLDS) + the `(name, ownerType=StackPanel)` composite identity for **StackPanel's own** orientation (11s + Rule 3 — HOLDS); the per-child measure offer (D-H — WPF `StackMeasureHelper` non-scrolling: horizontal offers `{∞w, constraint.h}`, vertical `{constraint.w, ∞h}` — VAML matches, and the S130 `RecorderLeaf` measure-offer assertions hold); the **DesiredSize accumulation** rule (D-H — WPF `stackDesiredSize.Width += child; Height = Math.Max(...)`; VAML matches modulo the 11ac S827 no-clamp finalize which 11ac owns); the non-scrolling FE-branch placement (11ab S824 — kept; the `StackPanel : Panel : IStackMeasure` re-base is THIS seat's own per Rule 3); the S2→S7 compiled parity (the S288 `DualPathParity` on an authored `<StackPanel>` doc). > ```csharp
> protected override Size MeasureOverride(Size constraint) {
>     Size childConstraint = new Size(Double.PositiveInfinity, Double.PositiveInfinity);
>     foreach (UIElement child in InternalChildren) { if (child == null) continue; child.Measure(childConstraint); }
>     return new Size();   // <<< always EMPTY
> }
> ```
> VAML's `Canvas::MeasureOverride` (Element.cpp) offers every child `Size::Infinite()` (correct, WPF-mirror) but then folds `DesiredSize = { max over children effLeft+w, max over children effTop+h }` (a bounding-extent accumulator, clamped ≥ 0, NaN-zeroed) — an INVENTED non-empty Canvas `DesiredSize` that does NOT match WPF's always-empty `new Size()`. Observable: a canvas of absolute children measures as the bounding extent in VAML, ZERO in WPF (so a Canvas inside a parent measures/arranges differently).
> - **D5 (MATERIAL + the EDGE-ANCHOR): the ARRANGE is missing the `Left-beats-Right` / `Top-beats-Bottom` edge-anchor + the WPF `Size`-return contract.** WPF:
> ```csharp
> protected override Size ArrangeOverride(Size arrangeSize) {
>     foreach (UIElement child in InternalChildren) { if (child == null) continue;
>         double x = 0; double y = 0;
>         double left = GetLeft(child); if (!double.IsNaN(left)) { x = left; }
>         else { double right = GetRight(child); if (!double.IsNaN(right)) { x = arrangeSize.Width - child.DesiredSize.Width - right; } }
>         double top = GetTop(child); if (!double.IsNaN(top)) { y = top; }
>         else { double bottom = GetBottom(child); if (!double.IsNaN(bottom)) { y = arrangeSize.Height - child.DesiredSize.Height - bottom; } }
>         child.Arrange(new Rect(new Point(x, y), child.DesiredSize)); }
>     return arrangeSize;
> }
> ```
> WPF resolves a child's position from `Left`/`Top` OR (when that axis is NaN) from `Right`/`Bottom` anchored to the Canvas's OWN `arrangeSize`, and returns the `Size`. VAML's `ArrangeOverride` hard-codes top-left `finalSlot.x/y` + `effLeft`/`effTop` only, never reads `finalSlot.width/height` for an edge anchor, and returns void (the 11ae S841 seat already re-seated the `ArrangeOverride : Size` return generically — Canvas itself never honors a Right/Bottom-anchored child). This square-grid derivation (`ceil(sqrt(n))`) is the entire observable identity of "a uniform grid of N items is a near-square" — with no `vaml::UniformGrid`, there is no `UpdateComputedValues` at all.

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S693 dep:S692 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\Track.cs` (read in full: the `ThreePiecePanel`/`UpdateComponent` 3-child visual list :64-139, the `RangeBase.Minimum/Maximum/ValueProperty.AddOwner(typeof(Track))` :216-281, `MeasureOverride` measuring ONLY the Thumb + zeroing the scroll axis when ViewportSize is set :365-379, the dual-mode `ArrangeOverride` with `ComputeSliderLengths` (ViewportSize==NaN) vs `ComputeScrollBarLengths` (the track HIDES when `desiredSize <= viewportSize`) + `CoerceLength` + `ThumbCenterOffset` + the reversed piece-order :376-690, `IsEnabledChanged` static override metadata :28-33, `OnPreApplyTemplate` auto-binding the parts to the templated parent (RangeBase/ScrollBar/Slider) :691-740), and the code VAML ships in `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` (`Track : FrameworkElement` :2008-2024: `Minimum`=0/`Maximum`=100/`Value`=0 Double DPs under owner `"Track"` + typed getters/setters) / `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (`Track` ctor :4866-4877 + `MeasureOverride` :5132-5180 returning a NOMINAL box `{availableW, availableH}` with NO `ArrangeOverride` at all)):** the S693 `[DONE]`-adjacent Track stub overstates fidelity on the exact surface the 11cd tail ("the next primitives-scrollbar stub audited/closed") names. Critically, **no sibling corrective sprint reaches it**: 11cf closes TickBar, 11cg closes ScrollBar — the `Track` base itself is untouched by all of them; 11as (Slider S1005) owns the `ValueFromDistance`/`Density` DELTA math at the Slider seat but NOT the Track-public value↔pixel virtuals + `ValueFromPoint`/`ThumbCenterOffset`; 11bo S1000 owns the `(name, RangeBase)` shared value-owner base but does NOT name Track's `AddOwner(typeof(Track))` re-home; 11bc S1076 owns the single `Track.Value → BindsTwoWayByDefault` flag but NOT the Track DP metadata or surface; 11cc closed RepeatButton (the `DecreaseRepeatButton`/`IncreaseRepeatButton` parts are RepeatButtons — CONSUMED) and 11cd closed Thumb (the `Thumb` part — CONSUMED) — but the ASSEMBLY of those parts into the WPF 3-child Track layout is THIS sprint's, and the 11bc S1070-S1077 "unassigned drift" sweep did NOT list Track. Each residual axis below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF `<Track>`/the scrollbar+slider track document and have it lay out + map value↔pixel as WPF does), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (STRUCTURAL — the headline) — the THREE-PIECE component surface is entirely ABSENT.** WPF `Track` maintains a `DecreaseRepeatButton`/`Thumb`/`IncreaseRepeatButton` slot triple + the `UpdateComponent(ThreePiecePanel)` 3-child visual list (`Track.cs:64-139`); `OnApplyTemplate` resolves the template parts and `OnPreApplyTemplate` auto-binds them to the templated parent. VAML's `Track` ships a `FrameworkElement` with three owner-"Track" Double DPs and a nominal `MeasureOverride` — NO component slots, NO 3-child list, NO template-part resolution, NO parent auto-bind. A corpus `<Track>` cannot host a Thumb + page RepeatButtons at all.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL — the layout) — there is NO `ArrangeOverride` and the `MeasureOverride` is wrong; WPF is a dual-mode track.** WPF `Track.ArrangeOverride` runs `ComputeSliderLengths` (when `ViewportSize.IsNaN`) placing the three parts ratio-derived across the track, OR `ComputeScrollBarLengths` (the SCROLLBAR mode) which **HIDES the track entirely when `desiredSize <= viewportSize`** (nothing left to scroll) and otherwise sizes the Thumb to the viewport fraction, both via `CoerceLength` + `ThumbCenterOffset` with the `IsDirectionReversed` piece-order swap (`Track.cs:376-690`). VAML has ZERO arrange logic. And `MeasureOverride` (`:365-379`) measures **ONLY the Thumb** (the track itself is zero in the scroll axis), whereas VAML returns a fixed box for the whole track.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL — the DP surface) — `ViewportSize`/`IsDirectionReversed`/`Orientation` + the metadata are absent.** WPF registers `ViewportSize` (owner `Track`, default `NaN`, `AffectsArrange`, `IsValidViewport` = `d >= 0 || NaN`), `IsDirectionReversed` (bool, default `false`, `AffectsArrange`, the reversed piece-order), `Orientation` (owner `Track`, default `Horizontal`, `AffectsMeasure`, `IsValidOrientation`), and the static `IsEnabledChanged.OverrideMetadata(...)` (`Track.cs:28-33`). VAML registers NONE of these (Orientation was re-owned at 11ca S1243 for StackPanel/ScrollBar/ToolBar/ToolBarTray but NOT Track).
> - **D8 (MATERIAL — the value↔pixel mapping) — `ValueFromPoint`/`ValueFromDistance`/`ThumbCenterOffset` are absent at the Track seat.** WPF `Track.ValueFromPoint(Point)` + `ValueFromDistance(double, double)` + the protected `ThumbCenterOffset` + the `Density = Range/Max(Maximum-Minimum, MinimumTrackLength)`-style delta model convert track px ↔ value (`Track.cs:429-570`); `ValueFromDistance/Density` is the EXACT math 11as S1005 quoted at the Slider seat — the Track-public value↔pixel virtuals + `ValueFromPoint` + `ThumbCenterOffset` are THIS sprint's. And the `(Minimum/Maximum/Value, RangeBase)` `AddOwner(typeof(Track))` re-home onto the 11bo range-owner base (`Track.cs:216-281`) is NOT named in 11bo.
> - **D9/D10 — the DP metadata + the template-parent auto-bind.** WPF `Value/Minimum/Maximum` `AddOwner(typeof(Track))` carry `AffectsArrange`, `Value` `BindsTwoWayByDefault` (11bc S1076 named the ONE flag); `OnPreApplyTemplate` (`Track.cs:691-740`) auto-binds the parts to the templated parent (RangeBase/ScrollBar/Slider) + the orientation + the value so the Track stands alone inside a control template — VAML has none of the DP metadata + no parent auto-bind.
> **HOLDS (D-H — the part that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened + pinned):** `Track : FrameworkElement` (NOT `Control` — the WPF base class holds, Track.cs; the concrete parts are the `RepeatButton`/`Thumb` `Control`s); the three owner-"Track" Double DPs `Minimum`/`Maximum`/`Value` abandon their OWNER to the 11bo `(name, RangeBase)` shared base but the `Value` numeric clamp/disposition (S484/11bo D2 coercion chain) is CONSUMED not re-authored; the `(name, ownerType)` composite identity (11s + Rule 3) holds throughout (the `(Orientation, Track)`/`(ViewportSize, Track)`/`(IsDirectionReversed, Track)` registrations are the 11s composite contract + the S805-class same-name/different-owner coexistence); `IsValidOrientation`/`IsValidViewport` range-gates THROW via the 11t `S810_1` disposition; the FrameworkElement-branch placement (11ab S824). FIX: (1) add an inheritance-change delivery in `DependencyObject` (the S039/S811 owner) that, for a DP carrying `PropertyFlags::Inherits`, re-resolves the effective value **on the two events that can change it** — (a) a visual-child link ADD/REMOVE (the S121 `UIElement` child list — hooked at the child-list mutate, covering both `SetValue`-seeded and template-instantiated subtrees) and (b) a `SetValue`/`ClearValue` of a LOCAL on an inheriting pair — and fires that DP's metadata `notifyChanged(oldEffective, newEffective)` (`PropertyMetadata.h:80-81`, the existing `with_changed` seam) for every descendant whose effective value actually changes; (2) honor `OverridesInheritanceBehavior` per `DependencyObject.cpp:474-477`/`:550-565` (the flag is already read + threaded — D2 consumes it, does NOT re-author the read); (3) dedupe: a subtree re-attached under an ancestor with the SAME effective value fires NOTHING (WPF's "real change" rule — the `oldEffective != newEffective` test, matching the `Set()`-time rule at `DependencyObject.h:61-64`); (4) depth-order the delivery PARENT-FIRST (WPF's tree-walk order) so a nested grip sees the final value once; (5) record in `DependencyObject.h` that this is the **descendant-push delivery restored as a REAL WPF-faithful mechanism** (S811 retracted a *fabricated* multi-subscriber pipeline; the inheritance-push is a genuine `TreeWalkHelper` behaviour and is NOT the retracted thing) — the annotation is mandatory so no future reader re-retracts it. WPF subscribes continuously (`StyleHelper` `OnTriggerSourcePropertyInvalidated`, `AddPropertyTriggerWithAction`) and un-fires when the trigger condition leaves the match. This is a **documented-but-not-delivered** behavior — a real conversion blocker (a WPF trigger that re-fires on a data change has no VAML equivalent).
> - **(c) Style/trigger setter values written as BARE LOCALS with no precedence band.** VAML's `StyleApplier` writes every setter value through S043 `Set` → a `local` on the object store, so: Trigger-vs-Setter precedence is write-order (not WPF's band ordering — `EffectiveValueEntry.cs:613-620`: `Local=11` > `StyleTrigger=7` > `TemplateTrigger=6` > `Style=5` > `ImplicitReference=8`), reverse-unfire is IMPOSSIBLE (a cleared trigger leaves its local behind; nothing can drop only the trigger's contribution), and no `ImplicitReference` band exists (an implicit style must beat an explicit style-setter, `ImplicitReference=8` > `Style=5`). > - **(d) Implicit-style key / scope / type drift.** (1) **Key:** WPF keys implicit styles on the actual **`Type`** — `FrameworkElement.cs:1867` `FindImplicitStyleResource(this, this.GetType(), ...)` + `ResourceDictionary.cs:2434` `HasImplicitStyles = (key as Type) != null` — VAML invents the string key `"Style:<TypeName>"`. (2) **Scope:** `FrameworkElement.cs:1080-1082` — implicit-style lookup **stops at the app**, never walks to system; VAML's `find_implicit_style` walks through system. (3) **Type breadth:** `type_name_of()` returns a name for only 5 hardcoded types (UIElement/StackPanel/Grid/WrapPanel/Canvas); every other concrete type (`Button`, `TextBlock`, …) returns `""` → no implicit style, where WPF resolves any type via `this.GetType()`.

(c) introduce a **real WPF precedence-band resolution** for styled / trigger / implicit setter values that supersedes the bare-local write: a styled property is resolved as `Local-wins > StyleTrigger > Style > ImplicitReference > default` (EffectiveValueEntry.cs:613-620), with a trigger's contribution applied/un-applied as a distinct band so reverse-unfire is possible, and setter vs trigger precedence is band-ordered (never write-order). (d) re-key + re-scope + widen the **implicit-style** surface: key on a Type token (owner-typed, per the 11s/11ak composite identity), scope stops at the app, and resolve for ANY registered element type (not a 5-type hardcode). ## Sprint 11an — S365 `{TemplateBinding}` RUNTIME residual closure: precedence band + converter + source-owner (the 11am-leaving gaps)  (goal: the S365 `[DONE]` TemplateBinding claim — "read of the templated control DP → live wire to the template part → re-skin on a control-DP change" — matches the actual WPF source on the THREE axes Sprint 11am names but does not fully own: the value lands in the real WPF `ParentTemplate` band, the binding carries WPF's `Converter`/`ConverterParameter`, and the control-side DP source resolves against the templated control's actual type, not a hardcoded owner)  [token S960+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S365 dep:S364 audit body is the S365 `SUPERSEDED`-leading note above; the 11am closure owns the visual-state/Storyboard rebase (S951/S953), `TargetType`/`ValidateTemplatedParent` (S950), the live OneWay `{TemplateBinding}` wire (S954), and the suite re-baseline (S955). 11an is the S365-specific RUNTIME residual that 11am's S954 establishes the wire FOR but does not itself close — three material axes from the WPF source, each a conversion blocker if left):**
> - **(a) The `ParentTemplate` value-source band is missing (D3).** WPF records a template-set value at the distinct `BaseValueSourceInternal.ParentTemplate` band — `FrameworkTemplate.cs:845` (`entry.BaseValueSourceInternal = BaseValueSourceInternal.ParentTemplate`), a **priority below `Local` (11) and above style-trigger (7)** per `BaseValueSourceInternal.cs` — so a TemplateBinding does NOT outrank an authored local, and a local DOES outrank a template value. 11am's S954 pushes the live value via `with_changed` but assigns **no band**, so the pushed value is indistinguishable from a local (the exact D4-class precedent error the state engine just fixed, now for the binding). 11an assigns the composite-identity value its real band.
> - **(b) `Converter` + `ConverterParameter` are dropped (D5).** WPF's `{TemplateBinding}` carries them — `FrameworkTemplate.cs:816-817` (`Converter = templateBindingExtension.Converter`, `ConverterParameter = templateBindingExtension.ConverterParameter`) — VAML's `SetterValue::TemplateBinding` / `templateBindings` carry only a property-name string and 11am does not route the wire through the existing S240-S251 converter pipeline. A faithful app whose template binding runs a converter (`Foreground` from a `Background`-derived brush, etc.) gets the unconverted value or nothing.
> - **(c) The control-side source-owner is hardcoded to `"UIElement"` (D6).** `apply_control_template` resolves the control-side DP via `DependencyProperty::ResolveForElement(controlProp, "UIElement")` — the literal owner string, regardless of the templated control's actual type (the S365 test uses a bare `UIElement`, masking it). WPF binds relative to the **real templated parent's** type and validates it (`ValidateTemplatedParent`). 11am's S950 validates TargetType and S954 fixes the PART (target) side owner; the SOURCE side resolution still hardcodes `"UIElement"`.

## Sprint 11ap — FontSize default fidelity + Linux platform capability documentation (the S400/S11k-1 `TextBlock.FontSize` default drift closure, plus the Linux guide note on the OS-derived default font size)  (goal: the `FontSize` control-base default is honestly WPF-real on Windows and DOCUMENTED as a Linux platform-capability difference exactly like the S11aj SystemColors precedent; the 11k-1 TextBlock-text sizing surface matches the real WPF source)  [token S975+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the 11k-1 `TextBlock`-re-base audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf` `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\SystemFonts.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\SystemParameters.cs`):**
> the 11k-1 re-base moved the `Text`→`TextBlock` text sizing surface onto the shared Control base, whose `FontSize` DP default is a **hardcoded `12.0` literal** (`src/core/src/Element.cpp` — `PropertyMetadata::WithDefault(Value::Double(12.0))` with the comment claiming it is *"the standard 96-DPI WPF message-font size … 12.0 DIPs — SystemFonts.ThemeMessageFontSize"*). The WPF source audit shows that claim is **an overstatement**: WPF's `FontSize` default is the `Control.FontSizeProperty` default **`double.NaN`**, and the *effective* default is derived at run time by `TextElement`/`System.Windows.Controls` from **`SystemFonts.MessageFontSize`** — `ConvertFontHeight(SystemParameters.NonClientMetrics.lfMessageFont.lfHeight)` (`SystemFonts.cs:414-421`) — which is an **OS/theme-derived value that is only ≈12.0 DIPs at exactly 96 DPI with the default classic message font**. It is NOT a constant, and WPF multiplies it by `ThemeManager.DefaultFluentFontSizeFactor` under the Fluent theme (SystemFonts.cs:422-434). VAML's comment/claim overstates fidelity: it presents a fixed literal as the faithful theme-message-font value.
> - **(D1)** The `FontSize` default is a hardcoded literal, not the OS-derived value the comment claims. On Windows the faithful value is `SystemFonts.MessageFontSize` (a real `SystemParametersInfoW`/`NonClientMetrics.lfMessageFont.lfHeight` query, natively linkable — the S11aj S923 precedent).
> - **(D2)** There is NO Linux analogue — Linux has no Win32 `GetSysColor`/`NonClientMetrics`-equivalent message-font API and no 1:1 theme feed, exactly the S11aj S923 hard-platform-limit finding for SystemColors. Linux carries the static `12.0` default ONLY (a documented platform-capability difference, never a silent NO-GAP to schedule).
>
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — mirror the S11aj GAP-C live-OS-query precedent, honoring Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit):** Windows (the WPF-commercial conversion target) derives the `TextBlock`/Control `FontSize` default from the **real OS message font** (native `SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_GETNONCLIENTMETRICS)` → `lfMessageFont.lfHeight` → `ConvertFontHeight`) — a real, live, native query with NO P/Invoke (VAML is C++), exactly as S11aj S923 wired the real `GetSysColor`/`SystemParametersInfoW` values + `WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE`/`WM_THEMECHANGED` refresh. **Linux** carries the static `12.0` default and is DOCUMENTED in the roadmap + the portability guide + the user guide as a **platform capability difference** (the "Linux default font size" guide note), exactly the S11aj S923 framing. **This is a DOCUMENTED SCOPE/PLATFORM decision, never a silent deferral** — the roadmap + guide are the authority, matching how S11aj closed SystemColors.
>
> **THE LINUX-GUIDE NOTE (the user directive — recorded here as part of the sprint):** the guide (and the roadmap) must state, in the same style as the other Linux platform-capability notes, that the **default font size** is: **Windows = the system/theme-derived message-font size** (≈12.0 DIPs at 96 DPI, live at run time); **Linux = the static `12.0` DIP fallback** (like the other things we do NOT dynamically handle on Linux that Windows does natively — the S11aj S923 SystemColors precedent). This is documented like the other Linux-not-supported/different items, not silently assumed.
>
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11u/11aa/11ab/11af/11ai/11aj/11ak/11al/11am/11an/11ao/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity; 11t owns the value-pipeline order + wrong-thread throw + validation disposition; 11aa the real WPF flag set; 11ab the UIElement-base drift (RenderTransform/Opacity/Visibility + the `FrameworkElement` layout-slot relocation); 11ai the `vaml::` exception base; **11aj owns the EXACT live-OS-query + Linux-platform-capability precedent this sprint mirrors (S11aj S920-S928 — SystemColors: native `GetSysColor`/`SystemParametersInfoW` on Windows, static defaults + documented-as-hard-platform-limit on Linux)**. 11ap is independent of 11s/11t/11u (no identity/pipeline/thread change); it is a small, self-contained FontSize-default fidelity closure that consumes 11aj's established platform-split pattern. 11z's executor seam untouched. ## Sprint 11av — S406 Focus/default-Button drift closure (WPF-faithful default-button via AccessKey + IsDefaulted DP + IsCancel/Escape + routed-key/InputBinding completeness WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S406 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "default-Button (an unconsumed Enter KEY-DOWN raises the default Button's Click — WPF-faithful; a handled Enter does NOT re-activate)" — matches the actual WPF source; the S406 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1025+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S406 dep:S405 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\ButtonBase.cs` + `...\Controls\Button.cs` + `PresentationCore\System\Windows\Input\AccessKeyManager.cs` + `...\Input\KeyboardNavigation.cs` + `...\Controls\Primitives\ToggleButton.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/FocusManager.cpp` / `Element.cpp` / `FocusManager.h`):**
> the S406 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on the exact surface its title names — the headline "an unconsumed Enter KEY-DOWN raises the default Button's Click via a FocusManager default-Button" is **not how WPF implements the default button at all**. Each facet below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a default-Button mechanism WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 — WPF has NO `FocusManager` `defaultButton_` slot; the default button is WPF's **AccessKey** mechanism on the `Button`.** WPF's default-Button behavior is: `Button.IsDefault` (`Button.cs` — `public static readonly DependencyProperty IsDefaultProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("IsDefault", typeof(bool), typeof(Button), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(BooleanBoxes.FalseBox, new PropertyChangedCallback(OnIsDefaultChanged)));`) → the change callback `AccessKeyManager.Register("\x000D", button); AccessKeyManager.Unregister("\x000D", button);` (`Button.cs`: register `"\x000D"` = Enter as an AccessKey on the Button). The read-only `IsDefaulted` DP is `IsDefault && KeyboardFocusWithinScope && !KeyboardNavigation.AcceptsReturn`, computed by `UpdateIsDefaulted`/`OnIsDefaultedChanged`. VAML's S406 ships a **per-tree `defaultButton_` member** (`FocusManager.h`) + a `set_default_button(Button*)` the caller inks in — **invented surface with NO WPF counterpart**. `DependencyProperty.FromName("IsDefault", typeof(Button))` never sees a vaml `defaultButton_` slot; there is no `IsDefault` DP and no `"\x000D"` access-key registration.
> - **D2 — the Enter activation is delivered at WPF `PostProcessInput`, not as a raw focused-element `KeyDown` inline path.** WPF `AccessKeyManager` (AccessKeyManager.cs) hooks `InputManager.PostProcessInput` (`OnInputEvent`, `PostProcessKeyboardInput`) and, for an unconsumed `Key.Enter`/`Key.Escape`, maps `text="\x000D"`/`"\x001B"` → `ProcessKey`, which runs `resolved key != null && !e.StagingItem.Input.Handled` then finds the access-key target — i.e. **after** the routed `KeyDown` handlers have run for that event (so a handler that handled the key prevents the default-button activation, the "handled Enter does NOT re-activate" premise) and through the global access-key table, NOT a per-FocusManager slot. VAML's `FocusManager::RaiseKeyRouted` raises `KeyDown` on the focused element, then if `!handled` calls `defaultButton_->raise_click()` — a same-call inline path with no `PostProcessInput` stage, so the WPF timing semantics (post-routed-handler, pre-acknowledged) are not reproduced.
> - **D3 — `raise_click`'s Command-then-Click ORDER is the known S401/11aq S981 inversion.** The default-button "raises the default Button's Click" inherits `Button::raise_click` (`Element.cpp:628-650`), which executes `source_command()` then raises `ClickEvent` (also the 11aq S981 defect). A WPF default-button Click handler observes the command's post-execute state; the vaml fallback observes pre-execute. Not owned by 11av (11aq S981 owns the order), but 11av must re-verify its default-button Click through the corrected order.
> - **D4 — `IsEnabled` command-coercion absent on the default gate.** WPF activates the default button only when it is enabled AND not command-suppressed (`UpdateIsDefaulted`: `!IsEnabled` → not defaulted + the ButtonBase `IsEnabledCore` command-coercion). VAML's `defaultButton_->raise_click()` checks `is_enabled()` (a standalone Int32 read) but has no `IsDefaulted`-analogue and no command-coercion — a disabled or command-unexecutable default button would still activate. Covered by 11aq S982's `IsEnabledCore` closure; 11av consumes it for the default gate.
> - **D5 — the `IsCancel` / Escape half is absent.** WPF `Button.IsCancel` registers `"\x001B"` (Escape) as the second access-key half of the default-button pair (`Button.cs OnIsCancelChanged`). VAML's S406 implements only the Enter/default half.
> - **D6 — the "tab order" overstates `KeyboardNavigation` fidelity (that part is 11ag S873's).** WPF tab order is `KeyboardNavigation`-driven (`IsTabStop` attached default **true**, `TabIndex` attached default `Int32.MaxValue`, `KeyboardNavigation.TabInto`/next/previous + TabScope). > `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Markup\XamlReaderHelper.cs` +
> `...\Markup\XamlReader.cs` + `...\Markup\XamlReaderConstants.cs`, and the code VAML ships in
> `src/core/src/ParsedElement.cpp` / `src/core/src/XmlScanner.cpp` / `src/core/src/XmlScanner.h`):** the S451 DONE marker's prose was accepted at face value
> (the exact failure mode the durable "WPF Source Audit Protocol" rule exists to catch), and the audit of the ACTUAL source found the document-grammar claim
> overstates fidelity on FOUR observable axes. Each is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture document-grammar behavior WPF does not
> have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL, the headline) — CDATA is DROPPED as if it were a comment; WPF treats CDATA as character TEXT content.** VAML's
>   `ParsedElement.cpp` drops `XmlTokenType::CData` IDENTICALLY to `XmlTokenType::Comment` (the `case XmlTokenType::Comment: case XmlTokenType::CData:`
>   fall-through at ParsedElement.cpp:270-274, with the S085/S451 doc comment "comments and CDATA are not tree nodes and are discarded"), and its own test
>   pins this (`ParsedElement_test.cpp` — `<a><!-- note --><![CDATA[ raw ]]><b/></a>` asserts `content.empty()` is TRUE). WPF does the OPPOSITE: CDATA is
>   **character data, real element content**, on BOTH paths — the TEXT path groups `XmlNodeType.CDATA` WITH `Text`/`Whitespace` and appends to the
>   element-content builder (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:1235-1238`), and the COMPILE path routes `case XmlNodeType.CDATA:` to `CompileText(...)` exactly like
>   `Text` (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:3790-3793`), where `CompileText` accepts CDATA and classifies it as whitespace-vs-content (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:5056-5060`).
>   So `<TextBlock><![CDATA[ raw ]]></TextBlock>` in WPF yields content `" raw "`; in VAML it yields EMPTY. Any WPF document carrying literal text in a
>   CDATA section (escaped `{Binding}` literals, `Run` text, non-trivial templates, whitespace-sensitive content) **silently loses that content** — a
>   functional conversion blocker, not cosmetic. **Comment is the ONLY thing WPF discards; CDATA is content.**
> - **D2 (minor) — root-element identity: the no-root / second-root error KIND is a VAML-invented parse contract.** WPF is a single-root system
>   whose stray/duplicate-root failure surfaces as a **well-formedness exception** from `System.Xml` (via `XamlReader` delegating the document grammar to
>   `XmlReader.Create`/`XmlTextReader`), NOT a document-contract `XmlParseException(UterterminatedElement)` at `(1,1)`. VAML's `parse_vaml`
>   (`ParsedElement.cpp:216-238`) throws its own `XmlParseException(UnterminatedElement)` on a second root and on no root — a narrower, re-worded contract.
>   Functionally harmless for well-formed docs (both refuse), but the error taxonomy/position is not a direct WPF mirror.
> - **D3 (minor) — the XML prolog is stripped but never VALIDATED as a well-formed XML declaration.** VAML's `strip_document_prologue`
>   (ParsedElement.cpp:33-72) consumes the BOM (EF BB BF) + leading whitespace + the first `<?…?>` without verifying it is a valid `<?xml version=…?>`
>   declaration and with no `<?…?>`-content safety. WPF's `XmlReader` REJECTS a malformed declaration (e.g. `<?xml` without a well-formed version
>   clause). For well-formed editor-saved files VAML matches; for superficially-shaped-but-malformed prologues VAML is **more permissive** than WPF.
> - **D4 (verified-consistent, the part of S451 that HOLDS) — BOM+prolog strip + comment-discard are correct; clr-namespace/xmlns/x:x- namespace resolution is
>   correct.** The strip is positioned at the SINGLE choke point both S2 text and the vamlcc recompile share, the comment-discard is consistent on both
>   paths, the canonical xaml namespace URI equals `XamlReaderConstants.DefinitionNamespaceURI`, and the `xmlns` declaration-vs-attribute + `x:`-directive
>   keyed-on-resolved-URI behavior matches WPF. D4 is re-verified + left intact, NOT re-audited as drift.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) **CDATA becomes real element
> content** on BOTH parse paths (S2 text + the vamlcc/VBamlReader compiled path) — a CDATA run is accumulated into the element's text content exactly like
> WPF (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:1235-1238 / 3790-3793`), ONLY `Comment` is discarded, and the S085/S086/S451 tests + the `ParsedElement.h`/`VBamlReader.h`
> doc comments are corrected (the `case XmlTokenType::CData` fall-through to the drop branch is REMOVED); (2) the **root-identity error** is re-cast as the
> well-formedness-disposition WPF produces (the reader reports the malformed-document failure through the established `XmlParseException` taxonomy but the
> S451 note's "document-contract second-root" framing is corrected to the WPF well-formedness reality + the position/taxonomy re-verified); (3) the
> **prolog strip is hardened** to WPF's declaration rule — a `<?` that does not parse as a well-formed `<?xml version=…?>` declaration is surfaced as a
> structured scan/parse error (matches WPF `XmlReader`'s rejection), never silently swallowed; (4) **D4** is pinned by an explicit parity test so the

> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the core defect) — the split DIRECTION is INVERTED: `split_property_element` uses `find('.')` (FIRST dot); WPF `SplitPropertyElementName` uses `LastIndexOf('.')` (LAST dot).** VAML's `split_property_element` (`ParsedElement.cpp:322-334`) does `const std::size_t dot = tagName.find('.')` and returns `{substr(0, dot), substr(dot+1)}` — the owner is everything BEFORE the FIRST dot, the property everything AFTER. WPF's `SplitPropertyElementName` (`XamlReaderHelper.cs:1652-1664`) does `int idx = longName.LastIndexOf('.'); ownerName = longName.Substring(0, idx); propName = longName.Substring(idx + 1);` — the owner is everything BEFORE the **LAST** dot, the property the LAST segment. So for `<Foo.Bar.Baz>` WPF resolves owner `"Foo.Bar"` + prop `"Baz"` (`DependencyProperty.FromName("Baz", Foo.Bar)`), while VAML resolves owner `"Foo"` + prop `"Bar.Baz"` — a real WPF document whose authored owner type carries a namespace dot (`clr-namespace` / `assembly:Type.Owner.Prop`, or a `Foo.Bar`-style type) is INVERTED under the first-dot split. The known WPF registered dotted-name DPs don't exist (composite keys are never dotted), so the common `<Button.Background>` one-dot form is unaffected — which is exactly why CI stays green — but any multi-dot authored owner flips owner/property and fires UnknownProperty for a different, wrong key. This is the same class of inversion the 11s/11u/11aa corrective sprints exist to close: the DONE marker's own example works while the grammar beneath it is wrong.
> - **D2 (label) — the DONE marker calls `<X.Prop>` "the S043 attached-aware path"; the actual mechanism does NOT distinguish WPF's OWNED (AddOwner) DP from an ATTACHED DP, so the label overstates fidelity for the very `<Button.Background>` case the title names.** `VamlReader.cpp:1212-1216` resolves the property through `lookup_dp_for_attr(propName, typeName)` — a composite `(name, owner)` read — with NO owned-vs-attached distinction. In WPF `<Button.Background>` is `BackgroundProperty.AddOwner(typeof(Button))` — a **shared, owned** DP (FrameworkElement.cs 「`BackgroundProperty`」 on Panel/Control's `BackgroundProperty`), NOT an attached DP. A faithful implementation must distinguish "the property is OWNED (AddOwner'd) by the element type" from "the property is ATTACHED (owner ≠ element, resolvable on any object)". VAML routes both through one composite lookup, so the "attached-aware" label overstates WPF fidelity on the exact owner-typed axis the 11s composite identity (S800-S808) governs.

## Sprint 11az — S454 STYLE-AUTHORING drift closure (the S454 `[DONE]` marker's authoring-grammar claim — `<Style TargetType BasedOn>` + `<Setter Property Value>` + `<Style.Triggers>` (PropertyTrigger/DataTrigger) authored into the live S362 model — checked against the ACTUAL WPF authoring grammar; the S454 drift the WPF-source audit recorded on the AUTHORING-GRAMMAR seat is closed; the *engine* axes S362/S363 close at 11ak/11al, 11ay owns the duplicate-`x:Key` indexer, 11az owns the S454 authoring grammar)  [token S1055+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S454 dep:S453 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\{Style,Setter,Trigger,DataTrigger,TriggerBase}.cs` + `FrameworkElement.cs` + `ResourceDictionary.cs`, and the S2 code in `src/core/src/VamlReader.cpp` `build_style`/`parse_setter`/`resolve_deferred_based_on`/`apply_implicit_style` + the `StyleAuthoring_s454_test.cpp` fixture):** the S454 `[DONE]` marker is accurate that the S2 reader authors `<Style>`/`<Setter>`/`<Style.Triggers>` into the live S362 model and fixes a real dangling-view bug (memoized `PropertyId` interning) — but the AUTHORING GRAMMAR drifts from WPF on the exact surface the title names, on FOUR observable axes. Each is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a Style authoring grammar WPF does not have, and must not refuse a WPF Style a commercial corpus `.xaml` actually contains — the S454 DONE note itself presented `PropertyTrigger`/`DataTrigger` as the authored element names while WPF's property-condition trigger element is `<Trigger>`, the same face-value acceptance the durable "WPF Source Audit Protocol" rule exists to forbid), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the WPF-doc-won't-load class) — VAML authors `<PropertyTrigger>`; WPF has NO such element; a corpus `<Trigger>` REFUSES TO LOAD.** WPF's property-condition trigger is the **`<Trigger>`** element (`Trigger.cs`), and WPF's canonical `<Style.Triggers><Trigger Property="IsMouseOver" Value="True">…<Setter …/></Trigger></Style.Triggers>` hits VAML's `build_style` `else throw unknown Style trigger child 'Trigger'` — a real WPF style fails to load. `PropertyTrigger`/`DataTrigger` as authored-element NAMES are VAML-invented (VAML's model types `PropertyTrigger`/`DataTrigger` map to WPF `Trigger`/`DataTrigger`; the WPF ELEMENT is `<Trigger>`). The S454 test only authors the VAML spelling, so CI stays green while the corpus spelling is refused.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — `<Setter>` authoring accepts any Property/Value with no authoring-time validation.** WPF `Setter.Seal`/`Setter.cs CheckValidProperty` REJECTS a setter target that is ReadOnly / `NameProperty` / `StyleProperty` / `UnsetValue`, and `Setter.SetterValueOfMarkupExtension` admits ONLY `DynamicResourceExtension` and `BindingBase` (`{TemplateBinding}` is NOT a BindingBase — it is rejected inside a Style/trigger setter, legal only in a ControlTemplate). S454's `parse_setter` captures a `<Setter Property="...">` with no authoring-time check, so a corpus setter WPF rejects parses silently (and a WPF-silent setter is accepted), and a `{TemplateBinding}` SetterValue is authored as a first-class Style value the engine will then reject at apply.

> `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\System.Xaml\System\Windows\Markup\StaticExtension.cs` + `TypeExtension.cs`, and the S461 code in
> `src/core/src/{BindingMarkup.cpp,VamlReader.cpp}` + `test/unit/MarkupStaticType_s461_test.cpp`):** the S461 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on
> TWO observable axes the audit caught, and the THIRD axis is the exact documented-architecture exception this sprint records, NOT closes. Each of the
> two that drifts is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a tokenization/type-identity scheme WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL) — the "WPF last-`:`-token lookup" claim is FALSE.** The WPF `{x:Static}` member format is `Prefix:Type.Member`, and the SPLIT is on the DOT, per `StaticExtension.cs`:
> ```csharp
> int dotIndex = _member.IndexOf('.');                     // FIRST dot
> string typeString = _member.Substring(0, dotIndex);       // "local:Constants" — the `:` prefix STAYS in
> ...
> fieldString = _member.Substring(dotIndex + 1, ...);       // "AppName"
> type = xamlTypeResolver.Resolve(typeString);              // the `:` is a NAMESPACE prefix the TYPE resolver consumes
> ```
> The colon is an **XML namespace prefix** consumed by `IXamlTypeResolver` (the S082 clr-namespace model), NOT a token delimiter. VAML's `ResolveStatic` (`VamlReader.cpp:3319-3333`) instead strips the LAST colon (`rfind(':')`, `str.substr(colon+1)` → a flat key `"Constants.AppName"`) and keys a registry on the colon-stripped remainder, with the code comment `// WPF-faithful token resolution` and the DONE parenthetical "WPF last-`:`-token lookup". Both are false — this is exactly the "accepted a label at face value" failure the durable WPF-Source-Audit rule exists to forbid.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL-ish, still a conversion blocker for TYPE IDENTITY) — `{x:Type Button}` returns a String, not a real Type object.** WPF `TypeExtension.cs` resolves and returns a REAL `Type`:
> ```csharp
> _type = xamlTypeResolver.Resolve(_typeName);
> if (_type is null) throw ...   // MarkupExtensionTypeNameBad
> return _type;                  // the Type object
> ```
> VAML's `ResolveType` returns `Value::String(it->second)` built from `register_type_value("Button","Button")` — the "type object" is the class-name STRING (`MarkupStaticType_s461_test.cpp` registers the String). The S461 title's "type object for TargetType / ContentControl binding" + the implicit-style Type-key (11al S943) + type-keyed resources therefore rest on a String, with no real Type identity.
> - **D2 — the EXCLUDED AXIS (the DOCUMENTED, ARCHITECTURE-JUSTIFIED MECHANISM REPLACEMENT, NOT closed here).** WPF `{x:Static}` FETCHES the static field/const/value by REFLECTION — `type.IsEnum → Enum.Parse` + `GetFieldOrPropertyValue` walking `currentType.BaseType`, plus the `MemberType` direct-type form (`StaticExtension.cs:92-131, :157-176`). VAML is a C++ translation with NO C# reflection, so a `{x:Static}` VALUE is app/reader-REGISTERED (`register_static_value`) rather than reflected. This is the mechanism replacement explicitly EXEMPTED: architecture-justified per the S250 "engineer wires, we bind" pattern (Rule 1 applies to the observable contract; the C++ registration value-path is the sanctioned adaptation). This sprint makes the TOKENIZATION of the static member (D1) + the TYPE identity of `{x:Type}` (D3) WPF-faithful, and it RECORDS D2 as the WPF-reflected-but-C++-registered surface — the enum-parse special-case, the base-type static walk, and the `MemberType` direct-type form are documented as the non-mirrored reflection surface, never silent.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close of D1 + D3; D2 stays the recorded exception):** (1) the static-member tokenization is re-written to the WPF first-dot grammar — split `{x:Static Prefix:Type.Member}` on the FIRST `.`, carry the `Prefix:` as a NAMESPACE prefix resolved through the S082 clr-namespace / namespace→type table (the type resolver), member = after the first dot; (2) a static member VALUE resolves against its OWNED (namespace-resolved) TYPE under the 11s composite `(name, owner)` + the 11al Type-token store — the flat colon-stripped single-key registry is retired; (3) `{x:Type}` returns a REAL Type identity (a `Value::Type` payload resolved through the composite/Type-token reader), replaced from `Value::String`, so TargetType/ContentControl/implicit-style/type-keyed-resource identity keys on a real Type; (4) D2 recorded as the sanctioned exception. Each closes the exact (non-exempt) drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held).
> **RELATION TO 11s/11t/11al/11af/11ai/11z:** 11s owns composite `(name, ownerType)` identity (S800-S808 — the owned-type key the static member + the Type identity resolve through); 11t owns the value-pipeline order + the strict-synchronous `with_changed` model; **11al S943 owns the Type-token implicit-style surface** (`FrameworkElement.cs:1867` — `{x:Type}`'s Type identity must key the SAME token store so `TargetType`/implicit-style/type-keyed resources agree); 11af owns the `PropertyPath` grammar (S845+, disjoint — the static member is a member path into a type, recorded not-opened); 11ai owns the `vaml::` exception base (the Class A unresolved/malformed static/type errors). 11bb is independent of 11s/11t/11u (no identity-key change, no pipeline-order change, no thread change) — it closes the S461-MARKUP-EXTENSION-SPECIFIC residual (D1/D3) ON TOP of those closures, exactly as the S-series siblings closed their S### residuals. **D2 is the recorded architecture-justified exception, NOT re-litigated — the value fetch stays C++-registered (S1068 is a record-only step).** ZERO new locks (ADR-018 — single-threaded registration + Set-time + resolve, the S126 affinity model unchanged).
