> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S463 dep:S462 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-Source-Audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Window.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\FrameworkElement.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Primitives\TextBoxBase.cs` + `System.Windows.Input\Extension\Mouse.cs` + `PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Markup\XamlReaderHelper.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/RoutedEvent.cpp` + `Element.cpp` (the authored-set event identities, `raise_loaded`/`raise_closing`/`raise_text_changed`, the S322 BindEvents table) + the event-tail routing in the VAML reader):** the S463 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on FOUR observable axes the audit caught — the exact "accepted a WPF-faithful label at face value" failure the durable WPF-Source-Audit rule exists to forbid, and each is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture an event identity WPF does not have, and must not represent an event WPF models very differently as a bubbling RoutedEvent), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL) — `Window.Closing` is NOT a Routed Event at all; it is a plain CLR event with `CancelEventHandler`.** WPF `Window.cs`: `public event CancelEventHandler Closing { add { Events.AddHandler(EVENT_CLOSING, value); } remove { Events.RemoveHandler(EVENT_CLOSING, value); } }` — a **plain CLR event** (signature `CancelEventHandler(object, CancelEventArgs)`), with **no `RoutedEvent`**, no route strategy, no `RaiseEvent`, and **no `handled` stop-flag**. It is raised via `OnClosing(CancelEventArgs e)` → `handler(this, e)` (Window.cs:2038-2041), and the args are `CancelEventArgs` with a `.Cancel` property (setting `e.Cancel = true` dismisses the window, Window.cs:2205). VAML's S463 registered `ClosingEvent` as a **Bubbling routed event** (`RoutedEvent.cpp:101-104`) raised through `RaiseEvent` with a `handled` return that the test even asserts. Two observables diverge: (a) the handler signature is `CancellableEventArgs`, not `RoutedEventArgs`; (b) there is NO route to bubble and NO `handled`-stops-anything — cancel is the dismiss, never a stop-flag. The `([DONE] ... Closing)` claim modeled a non-routed CLR event as a bubbling RoutedEvent — the direct analogue of the D-the-audit-checks writes, here on the Window.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — `Loaded` is `RoutingStrategy.Direct` + per-node tree broadcast, NOT Bubble.** WPF `FrameworkElement.cs:5699`: `public static readonly RoutedEvent LoadedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("Loaded", RoutingStrategy.Direct, typeof(RoutedEventHandler), _typeofThis);` — `Loaded` is **`RoutingStrategy.Direct`**, it does NOT travel the parent chain, and VAML's `raise_loaded()` bubbling the event UP to the Window's ancestors (`RoutedEvent.cpp:96` + the ancestor-climb in `Element.cpp`) inverts WPF. WPF raises `Loaded` by a **tree broadcast** — `BroadcastEventHelper.BroadcastEvent` (BroadcastEventHelper.cs:251-280) collects the whole loaded subtree and calls `fo.OnLoaded(args)` on EACH node individually (Direct, `new RoutedEventArgs(routedEvent, d)` per node with source == that node, BroadcastEventHelper.cs:262). So `Loaded` on a Window fires per-node across the loaded tree, never bubbles to an ancestor.
> - **D3 (MATERIAL) — `TextChanged` is Bubble (CORRECT), but the raise TRIGGER is wrong: WPF raises it on ANY text-content mutation, including a programmatic `Text` set; VAML raises it only from a key edit commit.** WPF `TextBoxBase.cs:901-906`: `public static readonly RoutedEvent TextChangedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("TextChanged", RoutingStrategy.Bubble, typeof(TextChangedEventHandler), typeof(TextBoxBase));` — Bubble (VAML's strategy matches). BUT WPF raises it from `OnTextChanged` called by `TextContainer.Changed` (TextBoxBase.cs:1395), which fires whenever the text content mutates, REGARDLESS of input source. VAML's `raise_text_changed()` fires only inside `handle_key` on a REAL edit commit (`Element.cpp:1637`), so `tb.set_text("x")` sets the Text DP and does NOT raise `TextChanged` — the exact ubiquitous WPF observable (a `Text="..."` assignment raises TextChanged) is missing for TextBox. (The S402 `Text` DP is `BindsTwoWayByDefault` per 11ar S991, but that is the write-back trigger, NOT the raise trigger.)
> - **D4 (MATERIAL) — the RAISED-ATTACHED `StackPanel.Button.Click` triple-dot form is NOT WPF syntax; WPF splits an attribute owner on the LAST dot and resolves the owner as a TYPE.** WPF `XamlReaderHelper.cs` `SplitPropertyElementName` (:1652-1664): `int idx = longName.LastIndexOf('.'); ownerName = longName.Substring(0, idx); propName = longName.Substring(idx + 1);` — so `StackPanel.Button.Click` resolves owner = `"StackPanel.Button"` + prop = `"Click"`, and `GetClrInfoForClass` tries to resolve a TYPE literally named `StackPanel.Button` (no such type) → WPF throws. The valid WPF attached-event form is TWO segments: `Owner.Event` where `Owner` is a type exposing a static `Add<Event>Handler(DependencyObject, handler)` (e.g. `Mouse.cs:151` `public static void AddMouseDownHandler(DependencyObject element, MouseButtonEventHandler handler)` → `Mouse.MouseDown="handler"`); and `Button.Click="handler"` is valid as an INSTANCE event (ButtonBase.cs:175 ClickEvent) ON the Button, never an attach on an ancestor. VAML's S463 invented a `Type.Owner.Event` triple-dot grammar (event-tail routing on the last dotted segment) that WPF does not have, filed "WPF-faithful bubbling attach" — the label is not supported by the source for that exact grammar. The INTENT (an ancestor capturing a child Button's bubbled Click) is real WPF (registering a bubbling handler on the ancestor / `AddHandler(Button.ClickEvent, ..., handledEventsToo)`), but the AUTHORING-GRAMMAR is a VAML original, not WPF markup.
> **HOLDS (D5 — the part of S463 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened):** `TextChanged` is genuinely Bubbling (D3's strategy half — VAML's S402/S463 Bubble registration matches `TextBoxBase.cs:901-906`); the S322 `BindEvents`/`register_event`/`bind_class_handler` markup-event wiring mechanism (a handler name resolved on the x:Class owner, a keyed event attribute routed, deferred-event resolution) is real and WPF-consistent for INSTANCE events; the `Button.Click` instance-event form authored ON a Button raises + bubbles correctly (S401/S324 flow); a child Button's raised `Click` bubbles to its ancestors through the routed engine. These are pinned by the parity test in this sprint.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) `Window.Closing` is re-modeled as a **non-routed, cancelable CLR event** (a `window_closing`-style `CancelEventHandler`-analogue carrying a `Cancel` bool; args authored with `CancelEventArgs`-faithful `.Cancel`; set-Cancel dismisses) — `ClosingEvent` is REMOVED from the bubbling `RoutedEvent` table, the `handled` stop-flag is retired for it, and the S322 markup event `Closing="..."` wires a CLR-Delegate subscription, not a routed handler (D1); (3) `TextChanged` gains the **programmatic-set raise** — `TextBox::set_text` (and any content-mutating setter) raises `TextChanged` exactly as `TextContainer.Changed` does, so `set_text("x")` fires it, on top of the existing key-commit raise (D3); (4) the **raised-attached authoring grammar is corrected** — the invented `Type.Owner.Event` triple-dot form is either (a) resolved to the real WPF `Owner.Event` two-segment attached-event form (an owner TYPE exposing a static `Add<Event>Handler`; for the Click case a real `Button.AddClickHandler(element, handler)`-style static that calls `UIElement.AddHandler(Button.ClickEvent, ...)`), or (b) — where WPF truly has no two-segment attached-event spelling — the VAML original triple-dot grammar is RECORDED as a VAML-ORIGINAL extension and RE-LABELED honestly, never "WPF-faithful" (D4). **The migration contract (commercial WPF → VAML with ZERO behavioral modification) is the standing authority: an authored WPF event attribute name + its WPF event identity (RoutedEvent name+strategy / CLR event) must resolve and fire exactly as WPF, and a corpus `.xaml` must never be edited to a non-WPF spelling.** Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 holds for the event identities — the RoutedEvent name is the authored key and the strategy is WPF-authored, never name-only-inferred).

## Sprint 11be — S464 COMMAND + CommandParameter WPF-drift closure (the authored `Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"` / `CommandParameter="{Binding SelectedItem}"` attribute surface actually routes to the ICommandSource execute; the parameter default is Null-not-empty-string; the MenuItem command object surface is one shared ICommand DP, not a dual string/object slot pair)  (goal: the S464 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "VamlReader::ExecuteCommand(name, parameter) resolves the app-registered command by name + gates on S246 CanExecute then invokes ICommand::Execute(Value); `Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"` supplies the command NAME; `CommandParameter` provides the parameter VALUE (bound path / static / literal); MenuItem.Header/Command/CommandParameter authoring rides the same attribute surface" — matches the actual WPF source on the ATTRIBUTE-TO-EXECUTE surface and the PARAMETER default, with the S464 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1087+]

> **THE S464 AUDIT RESIDUAL (quoted from the WPF ground truth, verified in the repo):** the S464 DONE marker's "attribute surface" claim is NOT what the code delivers. What exists is a **programmatic seam** — `VamlReader::ExecuteCommand(name, parameter)` (`src/core/src/VamlReader.cpp:3276-3296`) resolves the app-registered command by string name through the `commands_` registry, gates `CanExecute(parameter)`, then `Execute(parameter)`. That seam is arrow-straight WPF-faithful *in spirit* to `CommandHelpers.CriticalExecuteCommandSource` (`E:\GitRepos\wpf\...\PresentationFramework\MS\Internal\Commands\CommandHelpers.cs:120-138`: `parameter = commandSource.CommandParameter; ... else if (command.CanExecute(parameter)) command.Execute(parameter);`). ## Sprint 11bh — S470 DockPanel drift closure (live `LastChildFill` / WPF-faithful remaining-bounds Measure offer / DONE-marker honesty WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S470 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "`Dock` attached DP (Left/Right/Top/Bottom/Fill) + Measure/Arrange stacking children by dock order; classify_element → Solid" — matches the actual WPF source; the S470 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1106+]
> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S470 dep:S466 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\DockPanel.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` / `src/core/src/ElementDpFidelity.cpp`):** the S470 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on THREE observable axes, and its own title names one — "LastChildFill" is conspicuously absent from the delivered surface even though the marker claims "resolves the S462 DockPanel.Dock NO-GAP". Each axis below is a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must not manufacture a DockPanel WPF does not have), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — `LastChildFill` is REGISTERED but never READ: the ArrangeOverride hard-codes last-child-fill.** WPF's `DockPanel.cs` `ArrangeOverride` gates the fill on the real bool DP: `int nonFillChildrenCount = totalChildrenCount - (LastChildFill ? 1 : 0); if (i < nonFillChildrenCount) { switch (GetDock(child)) { ... } } else { /* fill child — the remaining interior */ }` — `LastChildFill` is a live `DependencyProperty.Register("LastChildFill", typeof(bool), typeof(DockPanel), ... default true)` (`DockPanel.cs` `LastChildFillProperty`). VAML's `ElementDpFidelity.cpp` registers `LastChildFill` (as `ValueType::Int32` default `1`, the "Bool via Int32" convention) but **no code path ever reads it** — `Element.cpp`'s `ArrangeOverride` uses a hard-coded `const bool isLast = (i + 1 == n)` fill test and there is no `last_child_fill()`/`set_last_child_fill()` accessor. So an authored `DockPanel LastChildFill="False"` (the WPF corpus bool form) resolves the DP but the panel STILL fills its last child — WPF would dock that last child to its `Dock` edge instead. This is the exact "registered-but-unconsumed" class of error the roadmap rails against elsewhere, and the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S649 DockPanel ×2 xaml instances]` gate stays green only because both placement classes exercise the default (true) fill.
> - **D2 (material-ish) — Measure offers children UNBOUNDED (`Size::Infinite()` on both axes); WPF offers the REMAINING (bounded) constraint.** WPF `DockPanel.cs` `MeasureOverride` builds the per-child offer as `childConstraint = new Size(Math.Max(0.0, constraint.Width - accumulatedWidth), Math.Max(0.0, constraint.Height - accumulatedHeight)); child.Measure(childConstraint);` then accumulates the docked child's `DesiredSize` into the track. VAML's `Element.cpp` `MeasureOverride` offers `Size::Infinite()` on BOTH axes (the header rationalizes it as "the S123 infinity rule") — so a child whose natural extent exceeds the panel's remaining offer is measured at its FULL natural size and never reports the panel's remaining bound, over-inflating `parentWidth`/`parentHeight` vs. WPF. (This is distinct from, and COMPOSES WITH, the 11ac S827 "DesiredSize may exceed available, not clamped" correction: S827 governs the Return value; D2 governs the OFFER handed into `Measure`. A wrap-to-available TextBlock offered `∞` wraps to content; offered the remaining bounds it wraps to the dock panel's leftover track — observably different.)
> - **D3 (claim/comment) — the header's "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM" label and the `Dock` enum comment overstate what shipped.** `Element.h` bills the unbounded-MEASURE + hard-coded-fill ARRANGE as "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM" while both diverge (D1/D2); and the `Dock` enum comment correctly notes "there is NO `Fill` member" (WPF `public enum Dock { Left, Top, Right, Bottom }` — correct) but frames fill as keyed position (`isLast`) which is only WPF-true when `LastChildFill == true` — a mechanism the code never consults. The `Dock` ATTACHED DP itself is WPF-faithful and HOLDS (D4 below).
> **HOLDS (D4 — the part of S470 that does NOT drift, recorded NOT re-opened + pinned):** the `Dock` attached DP matches the WPF source — `public enum Dock { Left, Top, Right, Bottom }` (NO `Fill` member — correct, `Fill` is positional via `LastChildFill`, not a `Dock` value); `DockProperty = DependencyProperty.RegisterAttached("Dock", typeof(Dock), typeof(DockPanel), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(Dock.Left, ...), new ValidateValueCallback(IsValidDock))` — owner `"DockPanel"`, default `Dock.Left`, range validator accepting exactly Left/Top/Right/Bottom (VAML's `with_validate(x>=0&&x<=3)` is the equivalent domain; the 11t S810_1 disposition makes an out-of-range authoring THROW `InvalidPropertyValueException`, matching WPF's `ArgumentException(InvalidPropertyValue)`); and the attach resolves on any object (S043, the `RegisterAttached` semantics). `classify_element → Solid` + the S470 DONE-marker's `(name, owner)` identity hold. These are pinned by an explicit parity test in S1108, never re-audited as drift.
> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) `LastChildFill` becomes a LIVE, READ surface: the `ArrangeOverride` gates the fill on the boolean `LastChildFill` exactly as `DockPanel.cs` (`nonFillChildrenCount = totalChildrenCount - (LastChildFill ? 1 : 0)`), the hard-coded `isLast` fill test is REMOVED, the DP is retyped to WPF's `bool` (the 11ar S990 "Bool not Int32" precedent), and a typed `set_last_child_fill`/`last_child_fill()` accessor lands — so `LastChildFill="False"` docks the last child to ITS dock edge; (2) the `MeasureOverride` offer is corrected to the WPF remaining-bounds `childConstraint` (`max(0, constraint − accumulated)` per axis), composing with the 11ac S827/S828 measure corrections, so a docked child measures against the panel's leftover track; (3) the "WPF-FAITHFUL ALGORITHM"/position-is-fill comment claims are corrected to the real mechanism (last-child-fill is a `LastChildFill`-gated DECISION, not a position invariant), history preserved un-edited per the S167_1 corrective convention. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`DockPanel.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — the `Dock`/`LastChildFill` DPs key `(name, ownerType=DockPanel)` per the 11s composite store).

## Sprint 11bi — S471 RadioButton drift closure (GroupName + logical-parent scope + sibling-Unchecked + never-uncheck WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S471 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "IsChecked + group semantics; routed Checked/Unchecked" — matches the actual WPF source; the S471 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1110+]

> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the headline) — `GroupName` (the actual WPF group mechanism) is entirely ABSENT.** WPF's exclusivity is keyed on the explicit string `GroupName` (`RadioButton.cs` `GroupNameProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("GroupName", typeof(string), typeof(RadioButton), new FrameworkPropertyMetadata(String.Empty, new PropertyChangedCallback(OnGroupNameChanged)))`), with `OnGroupNameChanged`/`Register`/`Unregister` moving the button into a **global thread-static `_groupNameToElements` weak-reference `Hashtable`** keyed by groupName, and `UpdateRadioButtonGroup()` unchecks name-grouped peers that share `KeyboardNavigation.GetVisualRoot(rb)`. VAML ships ONLY the empty-group single-parent model — there is **no `GroupName` DP, no `_groupNameToElements` registry, no named-group scoping anywhere** (`src/core` grep: zero `GroupName` hits), and the `Element.h` header comment defers it openly as NO-GAP. So a real WPF `.xaml` that authors `<RadioButton GroupName="ChoiceGroup"/>` cannot express the group at all — the S471 flat `✅ DONE` marker names "group semantics" while WPF's headline group mechanism does not exist.
> - **D2 (material) — empty-group scope is VISUAL-parent direct siblings; WPF is LOGICAL-parent children.** VAML `set_checked` (`Element.cpp:2988-3011`) clears `dynamic_cast<RadioButton*>` SIBLINGS under `parent()` (the immediate VISUAL parent). WPF's `UpdateRadioButtonGroup` empty-group arm walks `RadioButton` children of the **LOGICAL parent**: `parent = this.Parent; children = LogicalTreeHelper.GetChildren(parent);` — unchecking empty-group RadioButton children of the logical Parent. The two coincide only when the visual and logical trees are the same flat layer; under a logical parent that is not the immediate visual parent (or with non-RadioButton logical children between), VAML diverges observably from WPF.
> - **D3 (event-fidelity defect) — exclusive-clearing a sibling does NOT raise `Unchecked` on that sibling.** WPF's `UncheckRadioButton()` → `SetCurrentValueInternal(IsCheckedProperty, false)` flows through `ToggleButton.OnIsCheckedChanged` (the DP property-changed callback), so the previously-checked SIBLING raises its own `Unchecked` RoutedEvent with `source == that sibling`. VAML's `set_checked(true)` clears each checked sibling via a BARE `rb->Set(PropertyId::of("IsChecked","RadioButton"), Value::Int32(0))` (`:3006`) and calls `apply_change(value)` ONLY on `this` (`:3012`) — the cleared sibling emits **no routed event at all**. In WPF a handler on the cleared sibling's `Unchecked=` fires; in VAML it never does.
> - **D4 (click semantics) — the never-uncheck-by-click (`OnToggle`) contract is absent.** WPF `RadioButton.OnToggle()` always does `SetCurrentValueInternal(IsCheckedProperty, TrueBox)` — a second click on the ALREADY-CHECKED button does **NOT** uncheck it (unlike CheckBox, whose 11at toggle cycles). VAML's RadioButton has no `OnToggle`/click-wire in the S471 surface at all, and the 11at CheckBox toggle closure does NOT carry over (that is CheckBox's own click cycle). So the WPF-observable "a RadioButton in a group cannot be clicked off" contract is neither implemented nor recorded.

> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) introduce the real `GroupName` string DP (owner `RadioButton`, default `""`, `WithDefault(String)`) with WPF-faithful `OnGroupNameChanged` semantics — a global name→group registry of weak references (`_groupNameToElements`-analogue) into which a button `Register`/`Unregister`s on group-name change, and make exclusivity scope by `GroupName`: a NON-empty group resolves peers via the name registry sharing the visual root; the empty `""` group falls to WPF's LOGICAL-parent children walk (D2); (2) re-key the empty-group exclusivity off the visual-parent-siblings walk onto the LOGICAL-parent children arm — `parents chain` → `LogicalTreeHelper.GetChildren`-analogue walking the logical parent's RadioButton children so the scope matches WPF under a nested logical tree; (3) add the sibling `Unchecked` raise — when `set_checked(true)` clears a checked RadioButton sibling, that sibling raises its OWN `Unchecked` RoutedEvent (`source == that sibling`), exactly WPF's DP-callback path — so a handler authored on the cleared sibling's `Unchecked=` actually fires, and extend the `[11r EXHAUSTIVE: S661 RadioButton ×3 xaml instances]` gate to assert the sibling `Unchecked` fires (never green-on-CI for that axis); (4) add the `OnToggle` never-uncheck click path — a click on the checked button keeps it checked (WPF `RadioButton.OnToggle` = always-true), distinct from CheckBox's toggle (11at is NOT re-litigated; the 11ag/11aq click engine consumed, not re-authored). ## Sprint 11bj — S472 ComboBox drift closure (Selector/ItemsControl items model / object SelectedItem / SelectionChangedEventArgs payload / IsDropDownOpen dropdown surface WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S472 `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim — "ItemsSource/Items + SelectionChanged + dropdown interaction" — matches the actual WPF source; the S472 audit residual drift removed)  [token S1114+]

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S472 dep:S471 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\ComboBox.cs` + `...\Controls\Primitives\Selector.cs` + `...\Controls\ItemsControl.cs`, and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (ComboBox ctor + `split_items` at :3030-3180, `register_combo_properties`) / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h`):** the S472 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on the exact surfaces its title names, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF ComboBox document, not a comma-split string model), not recorded debt. The AUDIT SPLIT (recorded per the revised-audit discipline): the **content/editable chrome** sub-axis of ComboBox (the editable TextBox part + the `SelectionBoxItem`/`SelectionBoxItemTemplate` read-only DP surface) is recorded NO-GAP to the S649-list / 11k-11 generic content-owner routing continuation, NOT re-litigated here. 11bj owns ONLY what no other step owns — the items/selection/dropdown model:
>
> - **D1 — `ItemsControl`/`Selector` base + the `Items`/`ItemsSource` ITEMS MODEL is a comma-split String, not WPF's collection.** WPF `public class ComboBox : Selector` (ComboBox.cs:29), `public abstract class Selector : ItemsControl` (Selector.cs:26), `public class ItemsControl : Control` (ItemsControl.cs:34); `ItemsSourceProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("ItemsSource", typeof(IEnumerable), typeof(ItemsControl), ...)` (ItemsControl.cs:176) and the live `Items` is an **`ItemCollection`** (ItemsControl.cs:107), never a settable string DP. VAML registers `(Items, ComboBox)` and `(ItemsSource, ComboBox)` as **String** DPs split on commas/whitespace (`split_items`, Element.cpp:3039-3061) and ComboBox has NO `ItemsControl`/`Selector` base. A corpus `<ComboBox ItemsSource="{Binding MyList}">` or with multiple `<ComboBoxItem>` children cannot be represented. The S472-recorded deferral — "the WPF ItemCollection model is consumed at S649" — points at a **phantom token**: S649 was re-bound + resolved at 11k-11 as generic content routing, which does NOT schedule ComboBox's collection/selection model (the recorded NO-GAP is effectively not a real resolution point). The collection machinery that already exists in the repo (`ItemsControl.h`/`ItemsControl.cpp`, `ObservableCollection`/`CollectionView` from 11n-4, `ContentPresenter`+DataContext-inheritance from S500) is **not wired onto ComboBox**. (ListBox/ListView share the same `Selector` items/selection model — S473's residual is LISTED in the 11bj RELATION as a forward hand-off, closed here on the shared Selector base they both inherit.)
> - **D2 — `SelectedIndex`/`SelectedItem` are NOT owned DPs; `SelectedItem` is a String, not WPF's `object`.** WPF `SelectedIndexProperty` (Selector.cs:306, `typeof(int)`) + `SelectedItemProperty` (Selector.cs:362, `typeof(object)`) live on `Selector`; VAML ships a String `(SelectedItem, ComboBox)` synced from the flattened split list and no `(SelectedIndex, ComboBox)` int DP. A corpus `SelectedItem="{Binding x}"` binds an **object**; VAML stores only a String. Under the composite `(name, ownerType)` rule (Rule 3), `DependencyProperty.FromName("SelectedItem", typeof(Selector))` would never resolve VAML's `(SelectedItem, ComboBox)` — the 11s re-key touched the engine, not re-homed these DPs onto the `Selector` owner.
> - **D3 — `SelectionChanged` carries a BARE `RoutedEventArgs`; WPF's carries `SelectionChangedEventArgs` with the Added/Removed items.** WPF `SelectionChangedEvent = EventManager.RegisterRoutedEvent("SelectionChanged", RoutingStrategy.Bubble, typeof(SelectionChangedEventHandler), typeof(Selector))` (Selector.cs:75-76) with a `SelectionChangedEventArgs` exposing `AddedItems`/`RemovedItems` (the delta, source==the Selector). The five residual LABEL-SPECIFIC axes are each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML must be able to express a real WPF Label document), not recorded debt:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the sharpest, and Label's ONE named own-DP) — `Target` is typed String, but WPF's `Target` is a `UIElement` reference resolved via `NameReferenceConverter`.** WPF `Label.cs`: `public static readonly DependencyProperty TargetProperty = DependencyProperty.Register("Target", typeof(UIElement), typeof(Label), new PropertyMetadata((object)null), new ValidateValueCallback(Label.IsValidTarget));      [TypeConverter(typeof(NameReferenceConverter))] public UIElement Target { ... }` — `Target` holds the labelled `UIElement` **object**, resolved from a **name** by `NameReferenceConverter` (`<Label Target="myTextBox">` binds a reference, not a bare string). This is the exact same class as the ComboBox `SelectedItem`-String drift (11bj S1115, `Selector.cs:362` `typeof(object)`): the own-DP payload must be an object/reference, never a String.

## Sprint 11bl — S481 Border drift closure (Background AddOwner + interior fill / non-uniform BorderThickness / CornerRadius type + non-uniform corners / null-and-zero-thickness render-nothing / Affects* metadata WPF-fidelity)  (goal: the S481 `System.Windows.Controls.Border` `[DONE]` marker's fidelity claim matches the actual WPF `Border.cs` on EVERY axis the marker names and the S481 sprint pipeline delivered; the S481 audit residual drift removed end-to-end)  [token S1124+]

> **WHY THIS SPRINT EXISTS (the drift, recorded NOT silent — the S481 dep:S480 audit, per Rule 1 WPF-fidelity + Rule 2 WPF-source-audit, against `E:\GitRepos\wpf\src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\src\PresentationFramework\System\Windows\Controls\Border.cs` and the code VAML ships in `src/core/src/Element.cpp` (`register_border_properties`, `Border::MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride`) / `src/core/include/vaml/core/Element.h` (`Border`) / `src/presentation/src/VamlRenderer.cpp` (classifier emits `border_rect`) / `src/vulkan/src/ui/UiPipeline.cpp` (the S205 `border_style`/`border_coverage` authority)):** the S481 `[DONE]` marker overstates fidelity on FOUR observable axes, each a conversion blocker (a faithful VAML cannot express WPF's signature `<Border Background="...">` filled border, nor a non-uniform / null-brush / rounded-corner border the way WPF draws it), not recorded debt. The AUDIT SPLIT (recorded per the revised-audit discipline, Rule 3 held — the composite `(name, ownerType)` identity is correctly applied at S481, NOT re-litigated here): the **composite DP identity** (`Border.Padding` coexists with `Control.Padding`), the **single-child content slot**, and the **measure/arrange combined-deflation algorithm** (content deflated by `BorderThickness + Padding`, matching WPF `MeasureOverride`/`ArrangeOverride`) are WPF-faithful and recorded HOLDS (pinned in S1130). 11bl owns ONLY what no other step owns:
> - **D1 (MATERIAL — the core defect) — `Background` is entirely absent as a Border DP AND as a render surface; WPF Border both ADDS the `Background` owned-DP and FILLS the interior.** WPF `Border.cs`: `BackgroundProperty = Panel.BackgroundProperty.AddOwner(typeof(Border), ...)` (the `AddOwner` chain — `(Background, Border)` is an OWNED DP whose owner-type is `Border`), and `Border.OnRender` fills the interior (`dc.DrawRectangle(background, null, new Rect(ptTL, ptBR))` simple path; the complex `DrawGeometry(borderBrush-background split)` at the `_useComplexRenderCodePath` fold). VAML's `register_border_properties()` registers only `BorderBrush`, `BorderThickness`, `CornerRadius`, `Padding` — NO `(Background, Border)` DP, NO `set_background()`/`background()` accessor, and the classifier emits a bare hollow `border_rect` (a ring) with NO interior fill. An authored `<Border Background="...">` neither resolves as a Border-owned DP nor renders a fill. **Is it covered elsewhere?** S643a/S643b parse `Border Background="#80RRGGBB"` and carry a Brush ON the authored `(Background, Border)` DP-name the reader resolves under composite identity (11k-8/11k-9 list `Background` as a Border own-DP in the target tables), but NO sprint registers or renders it. **Conversion blocker:** a faithful VAML cannot express WPF's signature filled `<Border Background="...">`, and the renderer has no interior-fill path for it.
> - **D2 (MATERIAL) — non-uniform `BorderThickness` is collapsed to a single "representative" edge; WPF strokes each edge with its own pen + a complex-geometry path.** WPF `Border.cs` strokes each edge independently with its own cached pen (`LeftPenCache`/`RightPenCache`/`TopPenCache`/`BottomPenCache`) and uses a **complex geometry path** for non-uniform thickness + rounded corners (`_useComplexRenderCodePath = (!border.IsUniform || (cornerRadius != null && !cornerRadius.IsUniform) || ...)`). VAML's classifier comment says "a 4-edge thickness uses the top as the representative stroke" and `border_rect`'s `thickness01` is a single SCALAR — the S205 shader is a single-band SDF that CANNOT express per-edge thickness. `BorderThickness="1,2,3,4"` cannot be rendered WPF-faithfully.
> - **D3 (VALUE-TYPE + RENDER) — `CornerRadius` is typed as WPF's dedicated `CornerRadius` STRUCT, not a generic `Thickness`; and non-uniform corners are not representable.** WPF `Border.cs:148` registers `CornerRadiusProperty` `typeof(CornerRadius)` — a struct with `TopLeft`/`TopRight`/`BottomLeft`/`BottomRight` + `IsUniform` + the `IsCornerRadiusValid` guard that REJECTS negative radii. VAML registers it `ValueType::Thickness` (no four-corner semantics, no negative-rejection) and the S205 shader supports only a UNIFORM `radius01` scalar — non-uniform corners are not representable, and a negative CornerRadius does NOT throw the WPF validation.
> - **D4 (RENDER) — null/zero-thickness Border draws NOTHING in WPF; VAML forcibly draws an opaque black ring + a phantom 1px band.** WPF `Border.cs`: the default `BorderBrush` metadata is `(Brush)null` and `OnRender` gates the band on `if (!border.IsZero && (borderBrush = BorderBrush) != null)` — when `BorderBrush` is null OR `BorderThickness` is zero, WPF draws NO border band. VAML's default `BorderBrush` is a shared OPAQUE BLACK brush (`default_black_brush()`), so a bare `<Border>` draws a black ring where WPF draws NONE; and the classifier FORCES `thickness01` to **at least 1.0 when `bt.top == 0`** (`(bt.top > 0 ? bt.top : 1.0f)`), so a zero-thickness Border renders an artificial 1px band WPF would never draw. Neither is scheduled.
> - **D5 (METADATA) — the WPF `Affects*`/`SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` framework flags on the Border DP set are not carried.** WPF registers `Padding`/`CornerRadius` with `AffectsMeasure | AffectsRender`, `BorderThickness` with `AffectsMeasure | AffectsRender`, `BorderBrush` with `AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender`, `Background` with `AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender`. VAML registers all four Border DPs with `PropertyFlags::None`. 11aa S818 delivered the `Affects*` invalidation ENGINE + the honoring `FrameworkElement.OnPropertyChanged` seam, but no sprint applied those flags to the S481 Border set — a Border-DP change does NOT carry WPF's declared measure/render invalidation.
> - **D6-PIN (what HOLDS — recorded NOT re-audited as drift, pinned in the gate):** the composite `(name, ownerType=Border)` DP identity (Rule 3), the `BorderBrush`/`BorderThickness`/`Padding`/`CornerRadius` owner-name registrations under owner `"Border"` matching WPF `typeof(Border)`, the **single-child content slot**, and the **measure/arrange combined-deflation algorithm** — all WPF-faithful and pinned, NOT re-litigated.

> **THE DECISION (ratified at the head of this sprint — the contract forces full close, no scoped option):** (1) register `(Background, Border)` as an OWNED Brush DP via the `AddOwner` semantics of `Panel.BackgroundProperty` (the composite `(name="Background", owner="Border")` store key, per Rule 3 + 11s), with `set_background()`/`background()` accessors + `PropertyFlags::AffectsRender | SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` (11aa S818), and make the classifier emit the INTERIOR FILL (a `SolidRect` under the `BorderRect`, or extend `border_rect` with an interior fill at the WPF `new Rect(ptTL, ptBR)` deflated-by-border area); (2) non-uniform `BorderThickness` renders per-edge (the `border_rect`/`border_style` gained per-edge thickness + the complex-geometry path when `!IsUniform` OR non-uniform corners, mirroring `_useComplexRenderCodePath`); (3) `CornerRadius` is re-typed to a dedicated `CornerRadius` struct type (four corners + `IsUniform` + the `IsCornerRadiusValid` negative-rejection throwing per the 11t `S810_1` disposition) and non-uniform corners render via the complex-geometry path; (4) the null/zero-thickness render contract is honored — default `BorderBrush = nullptr` (WPF `(Brush)null`), the border band draws ONLY when `!IsZero && BorderBrush != null` (WPF `OnRender` gate), and the artificial `bt.top<1 -> 1px` fallback is REMOVED; (5) the Border DP set carries the WPF `Affects*`/`SubPropertiesDoNotAffectRender` framework flags consumed by the 11aa S818 invalidation seam. Each closes the exact drift; no invented surface is added; the WPF source (`Border.cs`) is the authority (Rule 1/Rule 2 held; Rule 3 held — all DPs key `(name, ownerType=Border)` per the 11s composite store).

## Sprint 11h --- 3rd-party IMPORT / INJECT seam  (goal: hard goal 3 — import and inject a 3rd-party control, proven in the viewer)  [token S520+]

> HARD GOAL 3 (sealed): to close out the lib we implement a means of importing 3rd-party libs and/or DLLs.
> Likely ONE sprint. We pick something we can put in a lib and INJECT, and the last step vaml_viewer shows the
> 3rd-party works.
> **FOREIGN-TYPE ACCESS MODEL (RECORDED DECISION — the "translation, not conversion" contract, resolved against
> the WPF source at plan review).** This is NOT a new sprint and NOT app-side conversion — VAML is a *reader*:
> it consumes the exact `clr-namespace:...;assembly=...` markup every in-box WPF app references, unchanged. The
> user's `.xaml` is NEVER edited to a "VAML format" — `clr-namespace` is already tokenized at S082 into
> `ClrNamespaceReference{clrNamespace, assembly}`; only the *resolution* of that reference is at issue, and it
> splits on whether the foreign type is platform-fixed or user-chosen:
> - **TIER 3a — IN-THE-BOX FRAMEWORK foreign types (LABEL-EQUIVALENT, in the LIB):** in-box reference-type
>   surface — `PresentationFramework.Aero2/AeroLite` (`SystemDropShadowChrome`), `System.Runtime`/`mscorlib`
>   primitives (`system:String.Empty`, `<system:Double>`, `<sys:Boolean>`), the `Microsoft.Windows.Themes`
>   types — is **platform-frozen, present in every WPF app, and NOT a NuGet choice**. It is the *same class as
>   `Label`*, which the lib already hardcodes as first-class. Therefore tier 3a lives in **vaml-core's S087
>   built-in registration table**, resolved **AUTOMATICALLY** — the same code path as `Label`, zero app action,
>   zero registration, zero install. This is the "access for free" path.
> - **TIER 2 — the RESOLVER SEAM (S520/11h), and TIER 3b — THIRD-PARTY toolkits (a plugin, NOT the lib):**
>   NuGet-package types (`DotNetProjects.Input.Toolkit` AutoCompleteBox, `MaterialDesignThemes.Wpf`) are
>   **unbounded + drifting + consumer-chosen** — the lib must NOT hardcode them (Label is platform-frozen; a
>   NuGet package is not). They resolve through the S520 `vaml::inject` seam: the app's `.xaml` STILL never
>   changes; only a deployment-side pluggable resolver (a plugin/new-repo mapping, registered into the seam)
>   supplies the type mapping. The 11h import/inject seam IS the access path; third-party is never in the lib,
>   never an app-side conversion.
> **ACCESS PATHS SUMMARY (authoritative):** in-box foreign types → automatic via the S087 built-in table
> (Label-equivalent, XAML never edited); third-party toolkits → the S520 resolver seam + a plugin (XAML still
> never edited). **No 11h "format" leaks into the app's files** — 11h is a resolver contract on VAML's side of
> the boundary, which is precisely the "not app, it's translation" principle. A separate GitHub repo / plugin
> data earns its keep ONLY for tier 3b (third-party vendors), gated behind the tier-2 seam.

## Sprint 11z — Injected-dispatcher interop + injected-dispatch wrap  (goal: the library runs inside a host message pump / dispatcher; the 3rd-party test + injected test dispatch CLOSE OUT the lib roadmap)  [token S540+]
> VIEWER GROWTH: this sprint's NEW renderable/interop proof = S545 (an injected test dispatch, triggered via the
> 3rd-party test hook, updates UI content LIVE in the viewer) — the anti-grave-whistle wrap that closes out the lib.
>
> DESIGN FRAME (consistent with the "we do NOT impose a dispatcher/async runtime" decision, ADR-006
> app-owned composition): **this library does
> NOT require a dispatcher nor use one.** It must function inside an ecosystem that DOES own one. The library
> therefore exposes a REPLACEABLE executor seam — `IUiExecutor` — that a HOST chooses to inject to claim
> ownership of the real UI thread's message pump. The question **"who owns the UI thread?"** is answered by
> the host: the default is library-driven (the framework drains its own queue via `IdleForOneTask`), but an
> app that already runs Win32/X11 pumps may inject `IUiExecutor` to drive our deferred work themselves. The
> executor is OWNED by the thread that owns the pump, exactly as the S037/S041/S143 thread-affinity model
> requires.
- S540 dep:S532  `IUiExecutor` (vaml/core, cross-platform) — the injectable UI-thread executor seam, the
      REPLACEABLE interop surface (a host injects it; the library never imposes a dispatcher). `NativeMessage`
      is an opaque cross-platform message carrier: Win32 = `MSG` (windows.h), Linux = `XEvent`-compatible
      backend struct `{ type, window, x, y, code, modifiers, timestamp }` (enum Type { other, mouse_move,
      mouse_button, key }); `#error Unsupported platform` for anything else. Interface: `UnhandledMsg(NativeMessage&)`
      (a native message the library did not handle, forwarded to the app to handle/forward), `IdleForOneTask()`
      (run AT MOST one ready task on the UI thread; return true iff one was consumed, false if none ready),
      `Awaken() noexcept` (THREAD-SAFE: wake the pump, including when it is waiting). REAL permanent public
      surface (NOT a STUB / NOT MINIMAL REAL), kept + extended by S541/S542. Absence of an executor = the
      library's own default pump behavior.
- S541 dep:S540  Windows pump adapter — `RunMessagePump(IUiExecutor*)`: the cooperatively-driven Win32
      message pump. Per turn: `PeekMessageW` (at most one) → `WM_QUIT` returns quit code → `WM_APP_WAKE_PUMP`
      (`WM_APP + 0x3A1`, posted by `Awaken()`) consumed as a wake (the work itself drains via
      `IdleForOneTask`) → `HandleLibraryMessage(msg)` if consumed else `executor->UnhandledMsg(msg)` (or
      `TranslateMessage`/`DispatchMessage` when no executor) → then `executor->IdleForOneTask()`. If nothing
      was ready, `GetMessageW` sleeps until a native message or `WM_QUIT` arrives — the cross-thread wakeup.
      The pure dispatch decision seams (the `processMessage` body) are headless-ctestable; the live pump is
      [both apps, not CI]. Completes the "an app that owns a Win32 pump can drive us" contract.
- S542 dep:S541  X11 pump adapter — `RunX11MessagePump(Display*, IUiExecutor*, X11Wakeup&)`: the
      cooperatively-driven Xlib/poll(2) pump. `X11Wakeup` is a self-pipe (pipe() in ctor, read-fd read side,
      `Signal()` noexcept write-one-byte from ANY thread — EAGAIN = a wake already pending, `Drain()` reads
      the pipe on the pump thread after readable; non-copyable). Per turn: `XPending`/`XNextEvent` (at most one)
      → `HandleLibraryEvent(event)` else `executor->UnhandledMsg(event)` (or `HandleDefaultXEvent` when no
      executor — Xlib has no generic Translate/Dispatch; routing unhandled events is app-specific) →
      `executor->IdleForOneTask()`. If nothing was ready, `poll(2)` on { xConnection, wakeup.ReadFd() } blocks
      until either an X event or a wake; poll error/hup → -1. The pure decision seams are headless-ctestable;
      the live pump is [both apps, not CI].
- S543 dep:S542  App-side executor consumable — the injected-executor consumer shape documented + proven:
      an `AppUiExecutor : IUiExecutor` (the X11 app side shown) holds an `X11Wakeup&`, `Awaken() noexcept`
      → `wakeup_.Signal()`, and supplies the app's `UnhandledMsg`/`IdleForOneTask`. Records the "who owns the
      UI thread?" contract: **an app that injects an executor OWNS the pump**; the library only drains via
      `IdleForOneTask()` and is woken via `Awaken()`. ADR-018: ZERO new locks — the wakeup is a lock-free
      signal (pipe write / posted thread message), the executor is single-thread-owned by the pump thread
      (the S037/S041/S143 affinity model). [ADR-006: the seam is app-owned + replaceable; the library does
      NOT ship an executor of its own.]
- S543_1 dep:S543  APP-OWNED-PUMP INBOUND SEAM — promote `HandleLibraryMessage(NativeMessage&)` (Win32) /
      `HandleLibraryEvent(...)` (X11) from internal pump helpers into PUBLIC library surface: the documented,
      headless-ctestable inbound entry an APP-owned main loop calls ONCE per native message/event, forwarding
      to the S540 `IUiExecutor` + draining via `IdleForOneTask()`/`Awaken()`. S541/S542 carry a one-line
      forward note (their internal call IS the body promoted public at S543_1 — supersede in place, no
      duplicate implementation). Records the pump-ownership contract with BOTH hosting modes: (1) VAML runs
      the pump (S541/S542) + calls the app's injected async (S540 `IUiExecutor`); (2) the APP runs the pump
      + calls the S543_1 inbound seam each message. ADR-018: ZERO new locks — single pump-thread owner, the
      S037/S041/S143 affinity model. NO-GAP: mode 2 becomes a named, resolvable contract, not an undocumented
      backdoor.
- S544 dep:S543  REFACTOR GATE(S11z): the injected-executor surface interops with the existing S323 input /
      S211 marshalling / S11z pump seams (a host may now drive our deferred work from its OWN
      pump, or keep our default); build + warning-clean + ctest GREEN both CI lanes (windows-msvc +
      ubuntu-clang); grep-audit: the `IUiExecutor`/`NativeMessage`/`X11Wakeup` seams are all REAL + consumed
      (no stub / no MINIMAL REAL / nothing orphaned). ADR-018: zero new locks sprints-wide.
- S545 dep:S544  INJECTED-DISPATCH WRAP (the hard-goal-4 close-out — the "calling the interface works" proof): the
